# Calc Optimizer — when to use

Source: https://tableau.github.io/tableau-ai-utilities/tableau-studio-skills/tableau-agent/calc-family/calc-optimizer

## What it does

Consumes a `calc_debug_handoff/1` payload from calc-debugger, or fires standalone on a perf ask. Reads the original formula, ranks it against the Performance Hierarchy, generates rewrite candidates in decreasing-tier order, filters candidates through the V-gate, authors the best surviving candidate via `author-calc`, verifies runtime equivalence on a scratch worksheet, and emits `calc_optimize_handoff/1`. Renders a locked Trade-offs block on every delivery.

## When to use it

Fires on "optimize this calc," "make this calc faster," "this calc is slow," "speed up this calculation," "why is this calc slow," "perf-tune this calc," or when a `calc_debug_handoff/1` arrives with a `perf_advisory` flag and the user says "now optimize it."

Do NOT invoke for writing new calcs (`calc-writer`), fixing broken/wrong-value calcs (`calc-debugger`), style/naming/house-style rewrites (`calc-linter`), cataloging calcs across a data source (`calc-inventory`), dashboard-level perf (`workbook-auditor`), or model/relationship perf (`join-and-relationship-advisor`).

# Calc Optimizer — SKILL.md

Source: https://tableau.github.io/tableau-ai-utilities/tableau-studio-skills/tableau-agent/calc-family/calc-optimizer/SKILL

# Calc Optimizer

## When to use (full trigger detail)

Optimize an existing Tableau calculated field for performance without changing its returned values. Consumes calc_debug_handoff/1 from calc-debugger or fires standalone on a perf ask. Ranks the calc against a locked 5-tier Performance Hierarchy, proposes a rewrite (or delivers an "already optimal" verdict), runs an 8-check Validation Gate plus a mandatory equivalence verification with fail-open, and emits calc_optimize_handoff/1. Perf-only scope. Correctness bugs route to calc-debugger; style/naming rewrites route to calc-linter. Triggers on "optimize this calc," "make this calc faster," "this calc is slow," "speed up this calculation," "why is this calc slow," "perf-tune this calc," or when a calc_debug_handoff/1 arrives with a perf_advisory flag and the user says "now optimize it." Do NOT trigger for writing new calcs (calc-writer), fixing broken/wrong-value calcs (calc-debugger), style/naming/house-style rewrites (calc-linter), cataloging calcs across a data source (calc-inventory), workbook-level perf tuning (workbook-auditor), or model/relationship perf (join-and-relationship-advisor).

## Purpose

Optimize one existing Tableau calculated field per run for performance, without changing its returned values. Delivers either a faster equivalent formula or an "already optimal" verdict backed by the Performance Hierarchy ranking. Runtime equivalence is verified before delivery.

## Trigger Conditions

Positive triggers: "optimize this calc," "make this calc faster," "this calc is slow," "speed up this calculation," "why is this calc slow," "perf-tune this calc," or arrival of a `calc_debug_handoff/1` payload followed by the user saying "now optimize it."

Do NOT trigger on the following adjacent asks. Refuse by exact slug.

| User ask | Route to |
|---|---|
| "Write a new calc for..." | `calc-writer` |
| "This calc is broken / returns wrong values / errors." | `calc-debugger` |
| "Rename this calc / rewrite for readability / house-style." | `calc-linter` |
| "List all calcs in this data source." | `calc-inventory` |
| "This dashboard is slow." | `workbook-auditor` |
| "This join / relationship is slow." | `join-and-relationship-advisor` |
| "Help me with a calc" (ambiguous). | `calc-orchestrator` |
| "Why was this calc optimized differently yesterday?" | Scripted prior-turn-diagnosis refusal (no visibility). |

## Scope Boundaries

- IN: rewriting one calc's formula for measurable performance improvement while preserving returned values; ranking the calc against the locked Performance Hierarchy; verifying runtime equivalence between original and optimized; emitting `calc_optimize_handoff/1`. Also IN: an explicit "already optimal" verdict with rationale when no meaningful rewrite exists.
- OUT: correctness fixes (`calc-debugger`); style, naming, house-style rewrites (`calc-linter`); new calc authoring (`calc-writer`); dashboard-level perf tuning (`workbook-auditor`); join/relationship model changes (`join-and-relationship-advisor`); optimizing across multiple calcs in one run (per-calc; multi-calc requires HC#1 opt-in); parameter, set, or hierarchy creation (platform gap).

### Edge-Case Boundaries

| Edge Case | Handling |
|---|---|
| Calc is already at top tier of Performance Hierarchy | Deliver "already optimal" verdict. Emit handoff with `fixed_formula == original_formula` and `optimization_tier_movement: none`. Never fabricate an improvement. |
| Optimization would trade perf for readability or grain-sensitivity | Deliver the rewrite plus mandatory Trade-offs block. Never omit trade-offs even for pure wins ("none surfaced" is a valid Trade-offs body). |
| Multi-source ambiguity on any referenced field | HC#4 one-clarifier. Name each candidate source with role and datatype. |
| User names multiple calcs to optimize | HC#1: ask "one at a time (default) or sequential this run?" before proceeding. |
| Original formula is broken (author-calc rejects, wrong values, missing field) | Refuse. Route to `calc-debugger`. Do not attempt optimization on a broken calc. |
| Equivalence verification fails twice | Fail-open per HC#8. Mark `verified_equivalent: false, sample_size: "verification_skipped"`. Deliver with warning. |
| `author-calc` hangs twice | Stop retrying. Check inventory. If not landed, hand off manual steps with "confirm when done." Matches calc-writer/debugger recovery pattern. |
| Rewrite candidate itself violates V-gate (e.g., R-LOD-02 nested LOD introduced) | Reject candidate. Try next tier down or deliver "already optimal." Never ship a rewrite that fails its own V-gate. |
| Perf-only rewrite would require model change (join, relationship) | Refuse. Route to `join-and-relationship-advisor`. Optimizer does not touch the model. |
| Calc has zero downstream references (unused calc) | Deliver the optimization anyway. Note `notes: "unused calc; consider deletion via calc-inventory audit"` in handoff. |
| Consumed `calc_debug_handoff/1` payload references a field that has since been deleted or renamed | Re-verify every field reference in the payload's `references.fields` list via `list-available-fields` at Phase 1 start. If any reference no longer resolves, refuse the optimization and route back to `calc-debugger` with a note: "handoff payload contains stale field references; re-run debugger against current data source before optimizing." Do not attempt silent substitution or partial optimization. |
| Scratch worksheet name collision (e.g., "Optimizer Scratch" already exists from a prior run) | Use fresh-name discipline: append `_v2`, `_v3` on collision. Never overwrite an existing scratch sheet. Clean up whichever name was used in Phase 8. |
| Datasource disconnects mid-optimization (any tool call fails with a connection error) | Stop immediately. Do not retry against a disconnected source. Report which phase was in progress and that no `calc_optimize_handoff/1` was emitted. Ask the user to reconnect before resuming. |

## Hard Constraints

- HC#1: Single-calc-per-run default. Multi-calc ask requires explicit user opt-in ("sequential this run") with one clarifier.
- HC#2: Value-preserving. Optimized formula MUST return the same values as the original for every group the original produces. Verified via mandatory equivalence check.
- HC#3: Locked 5-tier Performance Hierarchy in `skill-expertise/performance_hierarchy.md` is the ranking authority. Never invent a new tier or reorder tiers mid-run.
- HC#4: One-clarifier discipline. Ambiguous asks get exactly one combined clarifier, never chained.
- HC#5: No field, parameter, set, or hierarchy fabrication. If a rewrite would need a field that doesn't exist, refuse and ask.
- HC#6: No parameter, set, or hierarchy creation (platform gap).
- HC#7: Every delivery emits `calc_optimize_handoff/1` YAML unprompted with all required fields non-blank.
- HC#8: Validation Gate before delivery. 8-check gate identical to calc-writer/debugger, plus mandatory equivalence verification with fail-open on double failure.
- HC#9: Must read the original formula. If not pasted or resolvable from a `calc_debug_handoff/1` payload, ask for it.
- HC#10: Perf-only scope. If root cause of slowness is model-level (join, relationship, fanning), route to `join-and-relationship-advisor` before proposing a calc-side fix.
- HC#11: Locked Trade-offs block on every delivery. "None surfaced" is a valid body but the section header always renders.
- HC#12: Overwrite discipline. Default: author the optimized calc as `[original name] Fast`. Overwriting the original requires explicit user opt-in confirmation, which is never waived by user pressure ("just do it without asking").
- HC#13: Function signatures are looked up in `skill-expertise/INDEX.md` and its category files, never guessed. Same discipline as calc-writer and calc-debugger. If a rewrite needs a function that isn't in the library, drop that candidate and never invent a signature.

## Tools Used

- `list-workbook-datasources` — Phase 0 (identify target DS).
- `list-available-fields` — Phase 1 (verify all referenced fields exist; resolve AGG-flag for each).
- `resolve-field` — Phase 1 (resolve derivation prefix per field's actual AGG-flag; never string-match the formula).
- `author-calc` — Phase 5 (author the optimized calc).
- `get-summary-data` — Phase 6 (mandatory equivalence verification: author original + optimized on scratch worksheet, compare aggregated values).
- No file writes. Skill is compute-only; downstream consumers write.

## Performance Hierarchy (Locked, 5 Tiers)

Full catalog in `skill-expertise/performance_hierarchy.md`. Summary:

- **Tier 1 (fastest):** Boolean row-level, INT arithmetic, indexed field references, simple arithmetic on native measures.
- **Tier 2:** Aggregated arithmetic (`SUM(...) / SUM(...)`), single-dimension FIXED LOD, IF/ELSEIF on aggregates.
- **Tier 3:** Multi-dimension FIXED LOD, INCLUDE/EXCLUDE LOD, string equality checks.
- **Tier 4:** Nested LODs (depth 1), CONTAINS/STARTSWITH on non-aggregated strings, DATEDIFF in filter context, table calcs where a FIXED LOD would suffice.
- **Tier 5 (slowest):** COUNTD on high-cardinality fields, REGEXP_MATCH, nested LODs (depth 2+), row-level string ops inside aggregations, cross-datasource blending in calc context.

Every optimization delivery reports the tier movement: `optimization_tier_movement: {from: 4, to: 2}` or `optimization_tier_movement: none` for "already optimal."

## Phase Sequence

- **Phase 0.** Identify target data source. Multi-source ambiguity fires HC#4 clarifier with role/type disclosure.
- **Phase 1.** Read the original formula. Resolve every field reference via `list-available-fields`/`resolve-field`. Refuse silent substitution on missing fields (HC#5).
- **Phase 2.** Rank the original against the Performance Hierarchy. Note tier and specific slow-path flags (e.g., PA-COUNTD-HIGH-CARDINALITY, PA-REGEXP-IN-AGGREGATE).
- **Phase 3.** Generate rewrite candidates in decreasing-tier order (start from tier 1, work down). If original is already at tier 1 or is genuinely optimal at its tier, deliver "already optimal" verdict. Before keeping any candidate, look up every function it uses in `skill-expertise/INDEX.md` per HC#13.
- **Phase 4.** Filter candidates through the V-gate. Reject any candidate that itself violates a V-gate rule. Never ship a rewrite that fails its own gate.
- **Phase 5.** Author the surviving best candidate via `author-calc` as `[original name] Fast` (or overwrite the original only if user explicitly opted in per HC#12).
- **Phase 6.** Mandatory equivalence verification. Author both original and optimized on a scratch worksheet. Sample aggregated values by every dimension the original touches. Compare row-by-row. Fail-open on double failure per HC#8.
- **Phase 7.** Emit `calc_optimize_handoff/1` YAML unprompted with Performance Hierarchy movement, Trade-offs block, verification status.
- **Phase 8.** Clean up scratch worksheet.

## Validation Gate

Full spec in `skill-expertise/validation_gate.md`. 8-check gate identical to calc-writer/debugger:

- R-TYPE-01, R-TYPE-02: classification and return type match original.
- R-AGG-01, R-AGG-02: aggregation wrapping; ATTR two-condition rule.
- R-LOD-01, R-LOD-02, R-LOD-03: LOD syntax, nesting depth, filter order-of-operations.
- R-TC-01, R-TC-02: table-calc partitioning; prefer FIXED LOD.
- R-NULL-01: NULL handling explicit.
- R-BOOL-01: TRUE/FALSE/NULL, not 1/0/-1.
- R-PERF-01: no row-level string ops in aggregations.
- R-NAME-01: `[original name] Fast` default; ≤20 chars unless original was longer.

Plus one optimizer-specific check:

- **R-EQUIV-01:** optimized formula returns the same values as the original for every group the original produces. Verified via runtime equivalence check on scratch worksheet. Fail-open on double failure per HC#8.

## Verification Derivation-Prefix Rule

Resolve derivation prefixes from the calc's actual AGG-flag via `list-available-fields`/`resolve-field`, not by string-matching the formula for aggregation functions. A FIXED LOD pill placed on a shelf has AGG-flag `false` and gets `sum:` even though the formula string contains `SUM(...)`. String-matching would incorrectly force `usr:`.

## Domain-Accuracy Assertions (Locked)

These are directional rankings for typical extract-backed sources, not measured guarantees for every backend — see the Connection-Type Caveat in `skill-expertise/performance_hierarchy.md`. On live connections to pushdown-capable databases, the underlying engine's own optimizer can narrow these gaps.

- Boolean row-level calcs typically faster than aggregated boolean rewrites when the intent is a row-level flag.
- COUNTD is typically slower than SUM/AVG on the same field; the perf hit scales with cardinality.
- REGEXP_MATCH is typically slower than CONTAINS on the same string test; CONTAINS is typically slower than equality on an indexed field.
- FIXED LOD depth 1 is typically faster than FIXED LOD depth 2+; flatten wherever semantics allow.
- Filter-order-of-operations: FIXED executes before dimension filters (unless promoted to context); INCLUDE/EXCLUDE execute after. Optimizer must not silently change this relationship — this ordering rule is a fixed Tableau semantic, not a perf heuristic, and always holds regardless of connection type.
- Table calcs are typically slower than FIXED LODs that achieve the same semantics; rewrite to LOD wherever possible.
- Cross-datasource blending inside a calc is typically slower than reshaping the data model; if optimization would require this, route to `join-and-relationship-advisor`.

## Scale-Tier Branching

For workbooks with more than ~100 fields, batch `list-available-fields` in groups of ~10 with inline progress notes. For calcs with more than ~5 field references, resolve derivation prefixes in a single batched call rather than field-by-field.

## Multi-Calc Sequential Mode

Default: single calc per run. If user names multiple calcs, fire HC#1 clarifier: "one at a time (default) or sequential this run?" Sequential mode runs the full pipeline per calc, emits one `calc_optimize_handoff/1` per calc, and ends with a session summary.

Failure isolation: if calc N fails a hard constraint (e.g., HC#5 missing field), calcs 1..N-1 and N+1..M still ship. Session summary reports "M of N optimized. Failed: calc-X (reason)."

## Trade-offs Block (Locked)

Every delivery renders a Trade-offs section, even when empty:

- **Readability:** how the rewrite reads compared to the original.
- **Maintainability:** whether the rewrite is harder to modify later.
- **Grain-sensitivity:** whether the rewrite behaves differently under different view grains (FIXED vs. INCLUDE, filter-order-of-operations impact).
- **Downstream impact:** any peers (calc-debugger, calc-linter, calc-inventory) that would need to re-run.

"None surfaced" is a valid body for any subsection. Never omit the section header.

## Handoff Contract

Emits `calc_optimize_handoff/1` unprompted after every successful delivery (including "already optimal" verdicts). Full schema in `skill-expertise/handoff_schema.md`. Required non-blank fields:

- `schema_version`, `datasource_name`, `original_calc_name`, `original_formula`
- `optimized_calc_name`, `optimized_formula` (equals `original_formula` for "already optimal" verdicts)
- `optimization_tier_movement` (`{from: N, to: M}` or `none`)
- `trade_offs` (structured; every subsection has a body)
- `verified_equivalent` (true/false), `equivalence_sample_size`
- `perf_advisory` (advisory-only; never blocks)
- `overwrites_original` (true/false)

## Refuse to Fabricate

If any of the following can't be resolved, refuse and ask exactly one clarifier per HC#4:

- Original formula (HC#9).
- Data source (multi-source ambiguity).
- Referenced field, parameter, set, or hierarchy (HC#5).
- Whether user opts in to overwrite (HC#12).

Never guess. Never invent. Never fabricate a Performance Hierarchy tier or a function signature (HC#13).

## Graceful Degradation

These rules apply whenever something this skill needs is missing or fails. More specific rules elsewhere in this file take precedence.

- **Nothing to work on.** If no workbook is open, there is no data source, or the named calc, sheet, dashboard, or data source isn't found, stop before any other step. Say what you found (list the real names, if any) and ask the user to open the workbook or pick one. Never work on a guessed or closest-match target.
- **Tool call fails, times out, or returns empty.** Retry once, then stop retrying. Mark everything that depended on that call as not checked, continue with what you still can, and say which step failed. If the failed call was a write, stop and report the workbook's current state instead of continuing.
- **Partial results.** If any check, sheet, field, or data source wasn't evaluated, the summary says so (Partial: N of M checked; not checked: [list]). Never give a clean, ready, or PASS verdict on a partial run.
- **Reference file won't open.** Use the rules summarized in this file, say [file] unavailable; using the built-in summary, and never make up thresholds, rule IDs, or Desktop menu steps from memory.
- **Peer skill not installed.** If this skill would hand off to another skill that isn't available, say so and give the manual Desktop step instead. A handoff is never the only next step.
- **Platform gap.** If no tool can do something, say so plainly and give the manual Desktop path.
- **Failure messages.** Tell the user in plain language what was done, what wasn't, and the next step. No raw errors, stack traces, or JSON.
- **No fabrication.** Never invent fields, values, findings, or results to fill a gap left by a failed read.

# Calc Linter — when to use

Source: https://tableau.github.io/tableau-ai-utilities/tableau-studio-skills/tableau-agent/calc-family/calc-linter

## What it does

Consumes a `calc_write_handoff/1` / `calc_debug_handoff/1` / `calc_optimize_handoff/1` payload from any upstream calc-family peer, or fires standalone on a lint ask. Reads the original formula, runs it against the locked 12-rule catalog, groups violations by severity (error / warning / info), and delivers a report-only verdict by default. On explicit user opt-in, generates rewrite candidates, filters them through the V-gate, authors the consolidated rewrite via `author-calc`, verifies runtime equivalence, and emits `calc_lint_handoff/1`.

## When to use it

Fires on "lint this calc," "check this calc's style," "rewrite for readability," "does this calc follow our house style," "check my calc naming," "style-check this calc," or when an upstream handoff arrives and the user says "now lint it."

Do NOT invoke for writing new calcs (`calc-writer`), fixing broken/wrong-value calcs (`calc-debugger`), performance rewrites (`calc-optimizer`), cataloging calcs across a data source (`calc-inventory`), dashboard-level style tuning (`workbook-auditor`), or model/relationship naming (`join-and-relationship-advisor`).

# Calc Linter — SKILL.md

Source: https://tableau.github.io/tableau-ai-utilities/tableau-studio-skills/tableau-agent/calc-family/calc-linter/SKILL

# Calc Linter

## When to use (full trigger detail)

Lint one existing Tableau calculated field per run against a locked house-style catalog (naming, comments, indentation, structural clarity), report violations with severity + rationale, and optionally rewrite on explicit user opt-in. Style-only scope. Consumes calc_write_handoff/1 or calc_debug_handoff/1 or calc_optimize_handoff/1 from upstream peers, or fires standalone on a lint ask. Runs an 8-check Validation Gate plus a mandatory R-EQUIV-01 equivalence check on any rewrite. Emits calc_lint_handoff/1. Correctness bugs route to calc-debugger; perf rewrites route to calc-optimizer; new calc authoring routes to calc-writer. Triggers on lint this calc, check this calcs style, rewrite for readability, does this calc follow our house style, check my calc naming, style-check this calc, or when a calc_write_handoff/1 / calc_debug_handoff/1 / calc_optimize_handoff/1 arrives and the user says now lint it. Do NOT trigger for writing new calcs (calc-writer), fixing broken/wrong-value calcs (calc-debugger), performance rewrites (calc-optimizer), cataloging calcs across a data source (calc-inventory), workbook-level style tuning (workbook-auditor), or model/relationship style (join-and-relationship-advisor).

## Purpose

Lint one existing Tableau calculated field per run against a locked house-style catalog. Report violations with severity plus rationale, or (on explicit user opt-in) rewrite the calc to fix them. Style-only scope. Value-preserving.

## Trigger Conditions

Positive triggers: lint this calc, check this calcs style, rewrite for readability, does this calc follow our house style, check my calc naming, style-check this calc, or arrival of a `calc_write_handoff/1` / `calc_debug_handoff/1` / `calc_optimize_handoff/1` payload followed by the user saying now lint it.

Do NOT trigger on the following adjacent asks. Refuse by exact slug.

| User ask | Route to |
|---|---|
| Write a new calc for... | `calc-writer` |
| This calc is broken / returns wrong values / errors. | `calc-debugger` |
| This calc is slow / optimize this calc. | `calc-optimizer` |
| List all calcs in this data source. | `calc-inventory` |
| This dashboards style is inconsistent. | `workbook-auditor` |
| This join / relationship naming is inconsistent. | `join-and-relationship-advisor` |
| Help me with a calc (ambiguous). | `calc-orchestrator` |
| Why was this calc linted differently yesterday? | Scripted prior-turn-diagnosis refusal (no visibility). |

## Scope Boundaries

- IN: linting one calc per run against a locked house-style catalog; reporting violations with severity plus rationale; rewriting on explicit user opt-in with mandatory runtime equivalence verification; emitting `calc_lint_handoff/1`. Also IN: an explicit clean verdict when no violations surface.
- OUT: correctness fixes (`calc-debugger`); performance rewrites (`calc-optimizer`); new calc authoring (`calc-writer`); dashboard-level style tuning (`workbook-auditor`); join/relationship naming (`join-and-relationship-advisor`); linting across multiple calcs in one run (per-calc; multi-calc requires HC#1 opt-in); parameter, set, or hierarchy creation (platform gap); style-config file loading (skill uses only its locked catalog; user-supplied style files are out of scope).

### Edge-Case Boundaries

| Edge Case | Handling |
|---|---|
| Calc passes all style rules cleanly | Deliver clean verdict. Emit handoff with `violations: []` and `rewritten: false`. Never fabricate a violation. |
| User asks for lint but declines rewrite opt-in | Deliver report-only. `rewritten: false`. Never rewrite without explicit opt-in. |
| Rewrite would change returned values | Reject candidate. Try next rule down or refuse the rewrite for that specific violation. Report the violation without the rewrite. Never ship a value-changing style fix. |
| Multi-source ambiguity on any referenced field | HC#4 one-clarifier. Name each candidate source with role and datatype. |
| User names multiple calcs to lint | HC#1: ask one at a time (default) or sequential this run? before proceeding. |
| Original formula is broken (author-calc rejects, wrong values, missing field) | Refuse. Route to `calc-debugger`. Do not lint a broken calc. |
| Equivalence verification fails twice on a rewrite | Fail-open per HC#8. Mark `verified_equivalent: false, equivalence_sample_size: verification_skipped` for that rewrite. Deliver report + unrewritten violation with warning. |
| `author-calc` hangs twice | Stop retrying. Check inventory. If not landed, hand off manual steps with confirm when done. Matches calc-writer/debugger/optimizer recovery pattern. |
| Style violation is subjective (e.g., naming convention conflict between old-Superstore style and new-house style) | Report as `severity: info`. Never as error or warning. User decides. |
| Consumed upstream handoff payload references a field that has since been deleted or renamed | Re-verify every field reference in the payloads `references.fields` list via `list-available-fields` at Phase 1 start. If any reference no longer resolves, refuse the lint and route back to the upstream peer with a note: handoff payload contains stale field references; re-run upstream before linting. |
| Scratch worksheet name collision (e.g., Linter Scratch already exists) | Use fresh-name discipline: append `_v2`, `_v3` on collision. Never overwrite an existing scratch sheet. Clean up whichever name was used in Phase 8. |
| Datasource disconnects mid-lint | Stop immediately. Report which phase was in progress. Do not emit `calc_lint_handoff/1`. Ask user to reconnect before resuming. |
| Rewrite would violate value semantics via IF-to-CASE reordering, NULL propagation change, or short-circuit swap | Reject candidate at V-gate. Never ship a cosmetic rewrite that silently changes NULL/order semantics. Document in report as flagged but not rewritten: value-semantics risk. |
| S-NAME-* rewrite would rename a calc that other calcs in the same data source depend on | Tableau stores calc-to-calc references by internal ID (`[Calculation_...]`), so a caption rename does not break formulas inside the workbook. It can still confuse readers and break anything outside the workbook that cites the name (published-datasource consumers, external docs). Before authoring the rename, get the target calc's internal name from `list-available-fields` and search every formula for that internal name AND the caption. If any dependents exist, refuse the rename by default and report `notes: rename held: [N] calcs depend on this calc ([calc names]). Renaming won't break them in this workbook, but check published-datasource consumers and docs that cite the old name.` User can override with an explicit second opt-in. Never silent. |

## Hard Constraints

- HC#1: Single-calc-per-run default. Multi-calc ask requires explicit user opt-in (sequential this run) with one clarifier.
- HC#2: Value-preserving. Any rewrite MUST return the same values as the original for every group. Verified via mandatory R-EQUIV-01 equivalence check.
- HC#3: Locked house-style catalog in `skill-expertise/style_catalog.md` is the rule authority. 12 rules with severity tiers (error/warning/info). Never invent a new rule or reorder severity mid-run.
- HC#4: One-clarifier discipline. Ambiguous asks get exactly one combined clarifier, never chained.
- HC#5: No field, parameter, set, or hierarchy fabrication.
- HC#6: No parameter, set, or hierarchy creation (platform gap).
- HC#7: Every delivery emits `calc_lint_handoff/1` YAML unprompted with all required fields non-blank.
- HC#8: Validation Gate before delivery of any rewrite. 8-check gate identical to calc-writer/debugger/optimizer, plus mandatory R-EQUIV-01 equivalence verification with fail-open on double failure.
- HC#9: Must read the original formula. If not pasted or resolvable from an upstream handoff payload, ask for it.
- HC#10: Style-only scope. If root cause of the ask is correctness (calc-debugger) or performance (calc-optimizer), route by exact slug. Never absorb.
- HC#11: Report-mode default; rewrite requires explicit user opt-in. Lint this calc alone triggers report-only. Rewrite it to match or fix the style is the opt-in phrase. Never silently rewrite.
- HC#12: Rewrite discipline. Default: author the rewritten calc as `[original name] Clean`. Overwriting the original requires explicit user opt-in confirmation, which is never waived by user pressure (just do it without asking).
- HC#13: Function signatures are looked up in `skill-expertise/INDEX.md` and its category files, never guessed. Same discipline as calc-writer, calc-debugger, and calc-optimizer. If a rewrite needs a function that isn't in the library, drop that candidate and never invent a signature.

## Tools Used

- `list-workbook-datasources` — Phase 0 (identify target DS).
- `list-available-fields` — Phase 1 (verify all referenced fields exist; resolve AGG-flag for each). Default practice, not just the >100-field edge case: batch calls in groups of ~10 with inline progress notes whenever the workbooks field count makes a single call unwieldy.
- `resolve-field` — Phase 1 (resolve derivation prefix per fields actual AGG-flag; never string-match the formula).
- `author-calc` — Phase 5 (author the rewritten calc, only on user opt-in).
- `get-summary-data` — Phase 6 (mandatory R-EQUIV-01 verification: author original + rewrite on scratch worksheet, compare aggregated values). On a live (non-extract) datasource connection, this call is slower than on an extract; apply the high-cardinality sampling cap (top 200 + random 100) proactively rather than waiting for the >500-group threshold to be reached, to bound wait time.
- No file writes. Skill is compute-only; downstream consumers write.

## House-Style Catalog (Locked, 12 Rules)

Full catalog in `skill-expertise/style_catalog.md`. Summary:

**Naming (severity: error)**
- **S-NAME-01:** Calc name is ≤20 characters unless it inherits a longer parent name. A skill-added suffix (` Clean`, ` Fast`, ` Fixed`) doesn't count toward the 20.
- **S-NAME-02:** Calc name uses Title Case, no leading/trailing whitespace, no double spaces.
- **S-NAME-03:** Calc name is not a Tableau reserved word or a bare function name (e.g., SUM, COUNT).

**Structure (severity: warning)**
- **S-STRUCT-01:** IF/ELSEIF chains ≤4 branches; deeper chains flagged.
- **S-STRUCT-02:** Nested LODs deeper than depth 1 documented in a leading comment or flagged.
- **S-STRUCT-03:** Table calcs document partitioning/addressing in a leading comment or flagged.
- **S-STRUCT-04:** No unnecessary parentheses around single-token operands.

**Comments (severity: info)**
- **S-COMMENT-01:** Calcs longer than 5 lines have a leading comment explaining purpose.
- **S-COMMENT-02:** Non-obvious literal values (magic numbers, business thresholds) have inline explanatory comments.

**Formatting (severity: info)**
- **S-FORMAT-01:** Indentation uses spaces (2 or 4), consistent within one calc.
- **S-FORMAT-02:** No trailing whitespace on any line.
- **S-FORMAT-03:** One blank line max between logical sections.

Every violation is reported with its rule ID, severity, and one-line rationale. Rewrite suggestions render only when the violation is safely rewritable (see R-EQUIV-01 discipline below).

## Phase Sequence

- **Phase 0.** Identify target data source. Multi-source ambiguity fires HC#4 clarifier with role/type disclosure.
- **Phase 1.** Read the original formula. Resolve every field reference via `list-available-fields`/`resolve-field`. Refuse silent substitution on missing fields (HC#5). Re-verify any consumed handoff payloads references.
- **Phase 2.** Run the calc against the 12-rule catalog. Log every violation with severity + rationale.
- **Phase 3.** Assemble the lint report. Group violations by severity (error → warning → info). If zero violations, deliver clean verdict.
- **Phase 4.** If user opted in to rewrite (HC#11), generate rewrite candidates per violation. Filter through the V-gate. Reject any candidate that itself violates a V-gate rule or would change returned values. Before keeping any candidate, look up every function it uses in `skill-expertise/INDEX.md` per HC#13.
- **Phase 5.** Author the rewritten calc via `author-calc` as `[original name] Clean` (or overwrite the original only if user explicitly opted in per HC#12).
- **Phase 6.** Mandatory R-EQUIV-01 equivalence verification. Author both original and rewrite on a scratch worksheet. Sample aggregated values by every dimension the original touches. Compare row-by-row. Fail-open on double failure per HC#8.
- **Phase 7.** Emit `calc_lint_handoff/1` YAML unprompted with violations, rewrites (if any), and verification status.
- **Phase 8.** Clean up scratch worksheet.

## Validation Gate

Full spec in `skill-expertise/validation_gate.md`. 8-check gate identical to calc-writer/debugger/optimizer:

- R-TYPE-01, R-TYPE-02: classification and return type match original.
- R-AGG-01, R-AGG-02: aggregation wrapping; ATTR two-condition rule.
- R-LOD-01, R-LOD-02, R-LOD-03: LOD syntax, nesting depth, filter order-of-operations.
- R-TC-01, R-TC-02: table-calc partitioning; prefer FIXED LOD.
- R-NULL-01: NULL handling explicit.
- R-BOOL-01: TRUE/FALSE/NULL, not 1/0/-1.
- R-PERF-01: no row-level string ops in aggregations.
- R-NAME-01: `[original name] Clean` default; the original name part is ≤20 chars unless the original was longer. The ` Clean` suffix doesn't count.

Plus the optimizer-shared runtime check:

- **R-EQUIV-01:** any rewrite returns the same values as the original for every group. Verified via runtime equivalence check on scratch worksheet. Fail-open on double failure per HC#8. High-cardinality sampling cap (>500 groups → top 200 + random 100). Zero-dimension FIXED LOD read-gap recovery discipline preserved from calc-optimizer.

## Verification Derivation-Prefix Rule

Resolve derivation prefixes from the calcs actual AGG-flag via `list-available-fields`/`resolve-field`, not by string-matching the formula for aggregation functions. Preserves the runtime-lookup discipline confirmed in calc-writer/debugger/optimizer testing.

## Domain-Accuracy Assertions (Locked)

- IF/ELSEIF chain reordering can change short-circuit evaluation semantics. Never rewrite branch order without R-EQUIV-01 verification.
- IF-to-CASE conversion changes NULL propagation and equality semantics (CASE requires exact match; IF supports full comparison operators). Never do this rewrite unless the original formula is genuinely equality-only.
- Naming rewrites (S-NAME-*) never touch the formula body. Renaming is authoring a new calc with the new name, not editing.
- Comment additions never change formula semantics but can trigger `author-calc` reject if the comment syntax collides with formula syntax. Verify author-calc round-trip before delivery.
- Whitespace/indentation edits are semantically no-ops in Tableaus parser but must still pass R-EQUIV-01 as belt-and-braces.

## Scale-Tier Branching

For calcs with more than ~50 lines, batch the rule catalog into two passes: structural rules (S-STRUCT-*) first, then naming/formatting. For workbooks with more than ~100 fields (relevant when re-verifying handoff references), batch `list-available-fields` in groups of ~10 with inline progress notes.

## Multi-Calc Sequential Mode

Default: single calc per run. If user names multiple calcs, fire HC#1 clarifier: one at a time (default) or sequential this run? Sequential mode runs the full pipeline per calc, emits one `calc_lint_handoff/1` per calc, and ends with a session summary.

Failure isolation: if calc N fails a hard constraint (e.g., HC#5 missing field), calcs 1..N-1 and N+1..M still ship.

## Report Structure (Locked)

Every lint delivery renders this exact structure, even for clean verdicts:

- **Summary:** N violations found (X errors, Y warnings, Z info), or Clean — no violations.
- **Errors:** rule ID, rationale, snippet, rewrite suggestion (if safely rewritable). None surfaced is valid.
- **Warnings:** same shape.
- **Info:** same shape.
- **Rewrite delivered:** yes/no (only yes if user opted in AND R-EQUIV-01 passed).
- **Trade-offs (if rewrite delivered):** readability, maintainability, downstream impact. None surfaced is valid.

## Handoff Contract

Emits `calc_lint_handoff/1` unprompted after every delivery, including clean verdicts. Full schema in `skill-expertise/handoff_schema.md`. Required non-blank fields:

- `schema_version`, `datasource_name`, `original_calc_name`, `original_formula`
- `violations` (list; may be empty for clean verdicts)
- `rewritten` (true/false), `rewritten_calc_name` (only if `rewritten: true`), `rewritten_formula` (only if `rewritten: true`)
- `verified_equivalent` (true/false; N/A only if `rewritten: false`)
- `overwrites_original` (true/false)

## Refuse to Fabricate

Never invent a style rule outside the locked 12-rule catalog. Never fabricate a violation. Never silently rewrite. Never ship a rewrite that fails its own V-gate or R-EQUIV-01. Never invent a function signature (HC#13).

## Graceful Degradation

These rules apply whenever something this skill needs is missing or fails. More specific rules elsewhere in this file take precedence.

- **Nothing to work on.** If no workbook is open, there is no data source, or the named calc, sheet, dashboard, or data source isn't found, stop before any other step. Say what you found (list the real names, if any) and ask the user to open the workbook or pick one. Never work on a guessed or closest-match target.
- **Tool call fails, times out, or returns empty.** Retry once, then stop retrying. Mark everything that depended on that call as not checked, continue with what you still can, and say which step failed. If the failed call was a write, stop and report the workbook's current state instead of continuing.
- **Partial results.** If any check, sheet, field, or data source wasn't evaluated, the summary says so (Partial: N of M checked; not checked: [list]). Never give a clean, ready, or PASS verdict on a partial run.
- **Reference file won't open.** Use the rules summarized in this file, say [file] unavailable; using the built-in summary, and never make up thresholds, rule IDs, or Desktop menu steps from memory.
- **Peer skill not installed.** If this skill would hand off to another skill that isn't available, say so and give the manual Desktop step instead. A handoff is never the only next step.
- **Platform gap.** If no tool can do something, say so plainly and give the manual Desktop path.
- **Failure messages.** Tell the user in plain language what was done, what wasn't, and the next step. No raw errors, stack traces, or JSON.
- **No fabrication.** Never invent fields, values, findings, or results to fill a gap left by a failed read.

# Calc Hygiene Scan — when to use

Source: https://tableau.github.io/tableau-ai-utilities/tableau-studio-skills/tableau-agent/calc-family/calc-hygiene-scan

## What it does

Runs 8 rules against every calc: naming convention drift, missing author captions, unused calcs, excessive nesting depth, hardcoded values that should be parameters, deprecated function usage, cross-DS calcs without rationale, and over-reliance on LOD when a simpler pattern works. Tiers findings by severity, emits per-rule routing to calc-linter (autofix) or calc-optimizer (rewrite), and never mutates the workbook.

## When to use it

- "I want a workbook-wide calc hygiene sweep before publish."
- "I need to find unused calcs, hardcoded literals, and deprecated functions."
- "I want to route autofixable issues to calc-linter and rewrite candidates to calc-optimizer."

## When NOT to use it

- Not for explaining a single calc in plain language (route to calc-explainer).
- Not for documenting every calc in detail (route to calc-documenter for the full dictionary).
- Not for calc performance rewrites (route to calc-optimizer).
- Not for applying naming or hygiene fixes (route to calc-linter).
- Not for authoring new calcs from scratch (route to calc-writer).
- Not for diagnosing NULL returns (route to calc-debugger).
- Not for migrating a calc between datasources (route to calc-migrator).

## How to trigger it

- "calc hygiene scan"
- "audit my calcs"
- "check calc quality"
- "calc-hygiene-scan"
- "review my calcs"
- "calc quality audit"
- "find calc issues"

## Purpose

Audit every calculated field in a Tableau workbook against a locked 8-rule hygiene catalog. Read-only. Every finding is a manual Desktop-fix instruction; autofix candidates (naming drift, deprecated functions, hardcoded values) route to `calc-linter` via handoff signal but this skill never mutates. Opportunistically consumes `calc_documentation/1` handoff from `calc-documenter` with V5 formula-hash staleness detection; local-extract fallback when handoff is missing or stale.

## Trigger Conditions

- calc hygiene scan

## Do NOT Trigger On

- **IN.** One workbook per run. Read-only. 8-rule hygiene catalog. Opportunistic `calc_documentation/1` handoff consumption with V5 formula-hash staleness detection per portfolio-wide HC#15; local-extract fallback via `list-available-fields`, `resolve-field`, and formula pattern-matching. Autofix routing signal (`routing.calc_linter: true`) emitted for autofixable findings but never auto-invoked. Handoff schema `calc_hygiene_report/1`. Wide-workbook scale handling per HC#16.
- **OUT.** Any workbook mutation. Applying fixes (route to calc-linter). Explaining a single calc (route to calc-explainer). Bulk documentation (route to calc-documenter). Performance rewrites (route to calc-optimizer). Multi-workbook batch runs. Cross-workbook calc comparison.

## The 8-Rule Hygiene Catalog (Locked)

Every finding cites a rule ID. Multi-rule findings tier by highest severity. Full detection criteria, threshold defenses, and worked examples in `skill-expertise/rule_catalog.md`.

| # | Rule | ID | Severity | Signal source | Autofixable? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Naming convention drift | CH-NAMING-01 | Info | workbook XML | Yes (route to calc-linter) |
| 2 | Missing author captions | CH-CAPTION-02 | Info | workbook XML | No (author intent required) |
| 3 | Unused calcs (zero references) | CH-UNUSED-03 | Warning | reference graph (handoff) or local-extract usage scan | No (removal is destructive; route to calc-linter for delete workflow) |
| 4 | Excessive nesting depth | CH-NESTING-04 | Warning | formula parse | No (rewrite is out of scope for this skill; route to calc-optimizer) |
| 5 | Hardcoded values that should be parameters | CH-HARDCODED-05 | Warning | formula pattern-match against a locked hardcoded-value catalog | Yes (route to calc-linter) |
| 6 | Deprecated function usage | CH-DEPRECATED-06 | Warning | formula pattern-match against a locked deprecated-function list | Yes (route to calc-linter) |
| 7 | Cross-DS calcs without rationale | CH-CROSSDS-07 | Info | reference graph (handoff) with `cross_datasource_reference` flag | No (rationale is author intent; user acknowledges) |
| 8 | Over-reliance on LOD when a simpler pattern works | CH-LOD-OVERUSE-08 | Info | formula pattern-match against `skill-expertise/explanation_patterns.md` precedence rules | No (rewrite is out of scope for this skill; route to calc-optimizer) |

**Multi-rule tagging.** A calc can fire multiple rules simultaneously (common: CH-NAMING-01 + CH-CAPTION-02 both fire on a poorly-authored calc). Skill emits all triggered rule IDs in `rules_triggered[]`; severity tier set by highest match. Deterministic sort per HC#10: severity tier → rule ID ascending → calc name alphabetical.

**Fallback discipline (HC#5).** When rule detection depends on data thats unavailable (calc-documenter handoff missing, formula unreadable via `list-available-fields`), skill emits `unable to determine` sentinel per HC#5 for that specific rule on that specific calc.

## Workflow Phases

- **Phase 0 Scope.** Confirm workbook is open via `get-workbook-inventory`. If the call fails, returns no workbook, or the session is disconnected, stop and tell the user to confirm Tableau Studio is open with a workbook loaded — do not proceed to Phase 1 on an empty or failed inventory read. Ensure one workbook per run per HC#2. Enumerate calcs across all datasources via `list-available-fields`. If zero calcs exist, exit cleanly per HC#7 with no calculated fields defined; hygiene scan not applicable.
- **Phase 1 Handoff Discovery.** Check session context for `calc_documentation/1` handoff. If present, verify V5 formula-hash match per calc against current workbook state per HC#13. Populate `handoff_consumed` (true/false), `stale_handoff` (true/false), and per-calc `signal_source` flags. Stale handoff forces local-extract fallback per HC#13; skill does not render against stale data.
- **Phase 2 Rule Evaluation (numbered checklist).**
  1. For each calc in the workbook, apply each of the 8 rules from `skill-expertise/rule_catalog.md`.
  2. Formula text for parse-depth (CH-NESTING-04) and pattern-match rules (CH-HARDCODED-05, CH-DEPRECATED-06, CH-LOD-OVERUSE-08) comes from `list-available-fields`s formula field when populated for a calc; if a given calcs entry has no formula text, treat that calc as formula-unreadable for those rules and emit the HC#5 sentinel for them specifically rather than assuming the tool always returns formula bodies.
  3. Batch `resolve-field` calls in groups of 20 per portfolio-wide HC batching cap (matches calc-migrators Phase 2 pattern). If a batch call fails outright (timeout, disconnect), retry that batch once; on a second failure, emit `unable to determine` sentinel for every calc/rule pair depending on that batchs resolution and continue with the remaining batches — do not abort the whole scan.
  4. For each rule fired, populate `rules_triggered[]` with the rule ID, calc name, evidence citation, and `signal_source`.
  5. For autofixable rules (CH-NAMING-01, CH-HARDCODED-05, CH-DEPRECATED-06), set `autofixable: true` and populate `routing.calc_linter: true` at the finding level.
  6. For rules with unresolvable signals, emit `unable to determine` sentinel per HC#5 rather than skipping.
- **Phase 3 Severity Tiering + Deterministic Sort.** Sort per HC#10: severity tier (Warning → Info) → rule ID ascending → calc name alphabetical.
- **Phase 4 Validate.** Run the 5-check V-gate: rule coverage, per-calc signal-source attribution, ordering determinism, handoff completeness, autofix routing correctness. If any check fails, do not discard the run: re-run only the failing checks underlying data pull once (e.g., re-fetch signal-source labels for V2, re-sort for V3), then re-validate that check. If it fails a second time, deliver Tier A with the specific V-check named as unresolved and the affected calcs/rules listed, rather than blocking delivery entirely or silently passing.
- **Phase 5 Deliver.** Two-tier: compact Tier A chat summary with counts and top 5 Warning-tier findings; opt-in Tier B file save requires user path confirmation per HC#12.

## Hard Constraints

**HC#1 Read-only always.** Never mutates the workbook. Every finding is a manual Desktop-fix instruction plus (for autofixable rules) a routing signal to calc-linter.

**HC#2 One workbook per run.** Multi-workbook runs refused.

**HC#3 8-rule catalog locked.** No rule omitted, no fabricated rule added. Detection follows the criteria in `skill-expertise/rule_catalog.md`.

**HC#4 Refuse to fabricate.** No inferred naming conventions, no guessed author intent, no invented deprecation timelines. Sentinels: `null`, `unable to determine`, empty-state prose.

**HC#5 Sentinel discipline per rule per calc.** When a rules detection fails on a specific calc (formula unreadable, handoff stale for that specific calc), emit `unable to determine` sentinel for that rule on that calc. Other rules on the same calc still evaluate; other calcs still get all 8 rules.

**HC#6 Author caption preserved verbatim.** If a calc has an author caption or in-formula `//` annotation, CH-CAPTION-02 correctly clears (not fires). Skill supplements around author intent per portfolio-wide discipline.

**HC#7 Sentinel discipline for zero-calc workbook.** If workbook has 0 calcs, exit cleanly with no calculated fields defined message. Zero-datasource workbooks also exit cleanly.

**HC#8 Diff-mode transparency** (portfolio-wide HC#13). Repeat invocations against unchanged workbook + handoff state emit `diff_mode: reused_verbatim` in Tier A. Fresh-scan / reused-verbatim / targeted-rescan enum.

**HC#9 Ordering determinism** (portfolio-wide HC#14). Sort key locked: severity tier → rule ID → calc name alphabetical. Same input produces byte-identical top-5 and full findings list across runs.

**HC#10 Handoff-or-local labeled per calc per rule.** Every rule evaluation records `signal_source: handoff | local_extract | unresolved` per calc so downstream consumers know evidence origin.

**HC#11 Never silent file write.** Tier B save requires user path confirmation.

**HC#12 Autofix routing, never autofix invocation.** For autofixable rules (CH-NAMING-01, CH-HARDCODED-05, CH-DEPRECATED-06), emit `routing.calc_linter: true` on the finding. Skill never invokes calc-linter directly per HC#1; user opts in.

**HC#13 Handoff staleness detection required** (portfolio-wide HC#15). V5 formula-hash check per calc when consuming calc-documenter handoff. Per-calc mismatch forces local-extract fallback for that specific calc; other calcs with fresh hash-match still use handoff data.

**HC#14 Reference-file grounding.** All 8 rules cite detection criteria and worked examples in `skill-expertise/rule_catalog.md`. Threshold defenses (CH-NESTING-04 depth threshold, CH-HARDCODED-05 hardcoded-value catalog, CH-DEPRECATED-06 deprecated-function list, CH-LOD-OVERUSE-08 pattern precedence) all documented with empirical grounding.

**HC#15 Wide-workbook scale handling.** For workbooks with 50+ calcs, skill emits a wide-workbook-notice in Tier A (this workbook has N calcs; Tier A truncates to top 5 per severity tier, full findings list in Tier B). Per-calc evaluation still runs on every calc; only presentation truncates.

**HC#16 Case-insensitive resolve-field concern acknowledged.** `resolve-field` is case-sensitive (a known platform gap). CH-NAMING-01 detection uses handoff data preferentially when available; local-extract fallback exact-case matches per rule and does not attempt case-insensitive fuzzy matching.

## Validation Gate (5-Check)

- **V1 Rule Coverage.** All 8 rules evaluated against every calc in the workbook.
- **V2 Signal-Source Attribution.** Every rule evaluation per calc has `signal_source` populated.
- **V3 Ordering Determinism.** Findings sort key deterministic per HC#9.
- **V4 Handoff Completeness.** `handoff_consumed`, `stale_handoff`, and per-calc `signal_source` all populated.
- **V5 Autofix Routing Correctness.** Every autofixable finding (CH-NAMING-01, CH-HARDCODED-05, CH-DEPRECATED-06) has `autofixable: true` and `routing.calc_linter: true` set.

## Two-Tier Delivery

**Tier A (chat).** Compact summary: workbook name, calc count, findings by severity tier, top 5 Warning-tier findings with Desktop-fix instructions and autofix-routing flags where applicable.

Template:

```
**Calc Hygiene Scan: {workbook_name}**
Calcs evaluated: {N}
Findings: {N_warning} Warning, {N_info} Info, {N_sentinel} sentinel
Autofixable findings routing to calc-linter: {N}
Handoff consumed: {yes/no}, stale: {yes/no}
Diff mode: {fresh_scan | reused_verbatim | targeted_rescan}

Top 5 Warning-tier findings:
1. [{calc_name}] {rule_id}: {evidence}. Desktop fix: {manual_fix_instruction}. Autofixable: {yes/no}.
2. ...
3. ...

Routing offered: calc-linter (for autofixable findings), calc-optimizer (for CH-NESTING-04 and CH-LOD-OVERUSE-08).
Save full hygiene report to file?
```

**Tier B (opt-in file save).** Full report `.md` written to user-confirmed path per HC#11. Includes per-calc detail, per-rule evidence citation, Desktop-fix instructions, autofix-routing flags, and handoff YAML block.

## Handoff Schema

Emits `calc_hygiene_report/1`. Downstream: `calc-linter` (autofix for CH-NAMING-01, CH-HARDCODED-05, CH-DEPRECATED-06), `calc-optimizer` (rewrite for CH-NESTING-04, CH-LOD-OVERUSE-08), `workbook-auditor` (hygiene delta tracking).

Fields include: workbook (name, fingerprint), diff_mode, handoff_consumed, stale_handoff, calcs[] with per-calc rules_triggered / rules_cleared / sentinels / signal_source, totals (warning_count, info_count, sentinel_count, autofixable_count), routing_offered (calc_linter, calc_optimizer, workbook_auditor), v_gate results.

## Common Mistakes (Anti-Patterns)

- **Auto-invoking calc-linter.** HC#1 read-only + HC#12 routing-only. Skill emits `routing.calc_linter: true`; user opts in.
- **Silent stale-handoff rendering.** HC#13 requires per-calc V5 formula-hash check. Stale-per-calc forces local-extract fallback for that calc.
- **Rewriting author caption.** HC#6 preserves author intent. Skill supplements around it; never paraphrases.
- **Fabricating deprecation timelines.** HC#4. CH-DEPRECATED-06 uses the locked deprecated-function list in `skill-expertise/rule_catalog.md`; no inferred deprecation.
- **CH-NAMING-01 fuzzy-match on case-insensitive `resolve-field`.** HC#16 blocks. Exact-case per rule; no fuzzy matching to work around the shared-tool gap.
- **Silent file write on Tier B save.** HC#11 requires path confirmation.
- **Skipping a rule on a specific calc.** HC#5 requires all 8 rules evaluated per calc, with sentinel for unresolvable signals.

## Adjacent-Skill Routing

- **Upstream opportunistic:** `calc-documenter` (produces `calc_documentation/1` handoff).
- **Downstream opt-in per rule:**
  - CH-NAMING-01, CH-HARDCODED-05, CH-DEPRECATED-06 → `calc-linter` (autofix).
  - CH-NESTING-04, CH-LOD-OVERUSE-08 → `calc-optimizer` (rewrite).
  - CH-UNUSED-03 → `calc-linter` for delete workflow (destructive).
- **Downstream general:** `workbook-auditor` for hygiene delta across runs, `publish-readiness` for pre-publish hygiene sweep.
- **Refusal routes:** single-calc explanation → `calc-explainer`; performance rewrite → `calc-optimizer`; NULL diagnosis → `calc-debugger`; migration → `calc-migrator`; authoring → `calc-writer`.

## Known Limitations

- **Autofix out of scope.** Every autofixable finding emits routing signal; actual application is calc-linters job.
- **CH-LOD-OVERUSE-08 detection is heuristic.** Uses `skill-expertise/explanation_patterns.md` precedence rules; flags LOD-when-simpler-would-work but user acknowledges per finding.
- **CH-NESTING-04 threshold is heuristic.** Documented in `skill-expertise/rule_catalog.md` with defense.
- **CH-DEPRECATED-06 list is snapshot.** Deprecated-function list documented in reference file.
- **`resolve-field` case-sensitivity concern**. CH-NAMING-01 exact-case matches; no fuzzy fallback.
- **Cross-datasource references** in CH-CROSSDS-07 rely on handoff `cross_datasource_reference` flag when available; local-extract fallback flags cross-DS references but cannot verify rationale (author intent required).

## Graceful Degradation

These rules apply whenever something this skill needs is missing or fails. More specific rules elsewhere in this file take precedence.

- **Nothing to work on.** If no workbook is open, there is no data source, or the named calc, sheet, dashboard, or data source isn't found, stop before any other step. Say what you found (list the real names, if any) and ask the user to open the workbook or pick one. Never work on a guessed or closest-match target.
- **Tool call fails, times out, or returns empty.** Retry once, then stop retrying. Mark everything that depended on that call as not checked, continue with what you still can, and say which step failed. If the failed call was a write, stop and report the workbook's current state instead of continuing.
- **Partial results.** If any check, sheet, field, or data source wasn't evaluated, the summary says so (Partial: N of M checked; not checked: [list]). Never give a clean, ready, or PASS verdict on a partial run.
- **Reference file won't open.** Use the rules summarized in this file, say [file] unavailable; using the built-in summary, and never make up thresholds, rule IDs, or Desktop menu steps from memory.
- **Peer skill not installed.** If this skill would hand off to another skill that isn't available, say so and give the manual Desktop step instead. A handoff is never the only next step.
- **Platform gap.** If no tool can do something, say so plainly and give the manual Desktop path.
- **Failure messages.** Tell the user in plain language what was done, what wasn't, and the next step. No raw errors, stack traces, or JSON.
- **No fabrication.** Never invent fields, values, findings, or results to fill a gap left by a failed read.

# Calc Inventory — when to use

Source: https://tableau.github.io/tableau-ai-utilities/tableau-studio-skills/tableau-agent/calc-family/calc-inventory

## What it does

Fires standalone on a data-source-wide inventory ask, or consumes any upstream calc-family handoff (`calc_write_handoff/1` / `calc_debug_handoff/1` / `calc_optimize_handoff/1` / `calc_lint_handoff/1`) for single-calc catalog inclusion. Enumerates via `list-available-fields`, resolves derivation prefixes via `resolve-field`, fetches usage metadata via `get-workbook-inventory`, applies flag heuristics from calc-linter's and calc-optimizer's locked catalogs (read-only reference), computes complexity, reconciles batched pagination results, runs a 3-check read-only V-gate, and emits the handoff.

## When to use it

Fires on "list all calcs in this data source," "inventory the calcs," "catalog my calculated fields," "show me every calc in this workbook," "what calcs exist here," or when an upstream calc-family handoff arrives and the user says "add it to the inventory."

Do NOT invoke for writing new calcs (`calc-writer`), fixing broken/wrong-value calcs (`calc-debugger`), performance rewrites (`calc-optimizer`), style rewrites (`calc-linter`), data-model documentation (`data-model-documenter`), or workbook-level cataloging beyond calcs (`workbook-auditor`).

# Calc Inventory — SKILL.md

Source: https://tableau.github.io/tableau-ai-utilities/tableau-studio-skills/tableau-agent/calc-family/calc-inventory/SKILL

# Calc Inventory

## When to use (full trigger detail)

Catalog every calculated field in one Tableau data source per run into a scannable markdown table plus a machine-readable calc_inventory_handoff/1 YAML. Read-only. Records per-calc name, type, formula, reference graph (fields, parameters, sets, nested calcs), style/perf/complexity flags, and usage metadata (shelf placements, dashboard refs). Batched pagination for data sources with 20+ calcs. Consumes any upstream calc_write_handoff/1, calc_debug_handoff/1, calc_optimize_handoff/1, or calc_lint_handoff/1 for single-calc catalog inclusion, or fires standalone on a data-source-wide inventory ask. Routes bulk-fix asks to the appropriate peer (calc-linter for style, calc-optimizer for perf, calc-debugger for correctness) one at a time. Triggers on list all calcs in this data source, inventory the calcs, catalog my calculated fields, show me every calc in this workbook, what calcs exist here, or when a calc-family handoff arrives and the user says add it to the inventory. Do NOT trigger for writing new calcs (calc-writer), fixing broken/wrong-value calcs (calc-debugger), performance rewrites (calc-optimizer), style rewrites (calc-linter), workbook-level cataloging beyond calcs (workbook-auditor), or data-model documentation (data-model-documenter).

## Purpose

Catalog every calculated field in one Tableau data source per run. Delivers a scannable markdown table plus a machine-readable `calc_inventory_handoff/1` YAML. Read-only. Records name, type, formula, reference graph, style/perf/complexity flags, and usage metadata per calc. Batched pagination for 20+ calcs.

## Trigger Conditions

Positive triggers: list all calcs in this data source, inventory the calcs, catalog my calculated fields, show me every calc in this workbook, what calcs exist here, or arrival of any upstream calc-family handoff (`calc_write_handoff/1` / `calc_debug_handoff/1` / `calc_optimize_handoff/1` / `calc_lint_handoff/1`) followed by add it to the inventory.

Do NOT trigger on the following adjacent asks. Refuse by exact slug.

| User ask | Route to |
|---|---|
| Write a new calc for... | `calc-writer` |
| This calc is broken / returns wrong values / errors. | `calc-debugger` |
| This calc is slow / optimize this calc. | `calc-optimizer` |
| Lint this calc / check style / rewrite for readability. | `calc-linter` |
| Audit calc quality or hygiene (naming drift, unused calcs, deep nesting, hard-coded values). | `calc-hygiene-scan` |
| Document this data model / tables / relationships. | `data-model-documenter` |
| Audit the whole workbook (dashboards, worksheets, calcs). | `workbook-auditor` |
| Help me with a calc (ambiguous). | `calc-orchestrator` |
| Why was this inventoried differently yesterday? | Scripted prior-turn-diagnosis refusal (no visibility). |
| Bulk-fix / bulk-rewrite / bulk-lint all flagged calcs. | Route to appropriate peer per HC#10; never absorb as a bulk action. |

## Scope Boundaries

- IN: cataloging every calc in one data source per run with locked schema (name, type, formula, reference graph, style/perf/complexity flags, usage metadata); rendering scannable markdown table plus `calc_inventory_handoff/1` YAML; batched pagination for 20+ calcs; consuming any upstream calc-family handoff for single-calc catalog inclusion. Also IN: an explicit empty inventory verdict when the data source has zero calcs.
- OUT: authoring, rewriting, or deleting any calc (`calc-writer` / `calc-linter` / `calc-optimizer` / `calc-debugger`); cataloging across multiple data sources in one run (one DS per run; multi-DS requires HC#1 opt-in); tables/relationships (`data-model-documenter`); dashboard-level or workbook-level cataloging (`workbook-auditor`); parameters, sets, or hierarchies (cited as references, never resolved deeper); calc routing (calc-orchestrator); bulk mutations of any kind.

### Edge-Case Boundaries

| Edge Case | Handling |
|---|---|
| Data source has zero calcs | Deliver empty inventory verdict. Emit handoff with `calcs: []`, `total_count: 0`. Never fabricate calc entries. |
| Data source has 20+ calcs | Batched pagination in groups of ~20 with inline progress notes. Full inventory delivered at end. |
| Data source has 100+ calcs | Additional batching for `list-available-fields` in groups of ~10 as default practice. Note batching method in handoff. |
| Multi-source workbook | HC#1 clarifier: which data source? One DS per run. |
| Consumed upstream handoff payload has stale field references | Re-verify at Phase 1 start via `list-available-fields`. If stale, still catalog the calc but flag `stale_references: [field_names]` in that entrys metadata. Do not refuse the inventory over one stale entry. |
| Calc references a parameter, set, or hierarchy | Cite by name in `references.parameters` / `references.sets` / `references.hierarchies`. Never resolve deeper (thats out of scope). |
| Calc references another calc (nested reference) | List in `references.nested_calcs`. Build the reference graph across the whole inventory. |
| Calc has zero shelf placements or dashboard references anywhere in the workbook | Record `usage: { shelf_placements: 0, dashboards: [], flag: unused }`. Surface as a cleanup candidate in the summary. |
| User asks for bulk fix all flagged style violations | Refuse per HC#10. Route to `calc-linter` one calc at a time. Never absorb. |
| User asks for bulk optimize all tier-5 calcs | Refuse per HC#10. Route to `calc-optimizer` one calc at a time. Never absorb. |
| User asks for delete all unused calcs | Refuse; explain that calc-inventory is read-only and no calc-delete tool exists on this platform. Deletion is a manual Desktop step. |
| Datasource disconnects mid-inventory | Stop immediately. Report which batch was in progress and how many calcs were successfully cataloged so far. Do not emit `calc_inventory_handoff/1`. Ask user to reconnect. |
| Very wide data source (>100 fields, unrelated to calc count) | Batch `list-available-fields` in ~10-field groups with inline progress notes; locked threshold is field count > 30. Same discipline as calc-linter. |
| Multi-source workbook, user explicitly opts into cataloging all data sources in one run | HC#1 sequential-mode opt-in: after the clarifier, if the user confirms all of them, run Phase 0-7 sequentially per data source (one inventory + one handoff per DS, never merged into a single cross-DS entry list). Announce which DS is being processed before each pass. Default without explicit opt-in remains one DS per run. |
| Style/perf/complexity flag heuristics come from `skill-expertise/style_catalog.md` and `skill-expertise/performance_hierarchy.md` | Read-only reference; never redefine or extend those catalogs mid-run. Cite rule IDs (S-*, PA-*) directly. |
| Usage-metadata tool unavailable (`get-workbook-inventory` returns error) | Proceed without usage data. Flag each calcs `usage` block as `unavailable_this_run: true` and note in handoff `notes`. Do not fabricate placements. |

## Hard Constraints

- HC#1: Single-data-source-per-run default. Multi-source workbooks require explicit clarifier before proceeding. User may opt into sequential all-data-source mode after the clarifier (yes, all of them) — runs one full inventory pass per DS, never merged, never skipping the clarifier itself.
- HC#2: Read-only. Zero mutating tool calls on the workbook or any calc. No `author-calc`, no calc renames, no deletions. Compute-only.
- HC#3: Locked schema in `skill-expertise/catalog_schema.md` is the per-calc entry authority. Never invent an attribute or reshape entries mid-run.
- HC#4: One-clarifier discipline. Ambiguous asks get exactly one combined clarifier, never chained.
- HC#5: No calc fabrication. Every entry in the inventory MUST correspond to a real calc resolvable via `list-available-fields`. Never invent calcs to fill perceived gaps.
- HC#6: No parameter/set/hierarchy deep resolution. Cite by name only. Thats `calc-writer`s or the users job to resolve.
- HC#7: Every delivery emits `calc_inventory_handoff/1` YAML unprompted with all required fields non-blank. Even the empty inventory verdict.
- HC#8: Read-only V-gate before delivery. Verify (a) every catalog entry has all required fields populated, (b) batched pagination results reconciled into a single deduplicated inventory, (c) reference-graph is internally consistent (nested-calc references resolve to actual calcs in the inventory or are flagged as `external_reference: true`).
- HC#9: Must read live data source state. If `list-available-fields` unavailable, refuse the inventory and route to user for a reconnect. Never inventory from stale cache.
- HC#10: Cataloging-only scope. Bulk-fix asks route by exact slug (calc-linter, calc-optimizer, calc-debugger) one calc at a time. Never absorb bulk actions.
- HC#11: Flag heuristics are read-only references from calc-linter and calc-optimizer catalogs. Never extend or redefine those catalogs mid-run; cite rule IDs directly.
- HC#12: Batched pagination is default for 20+ calcs. Inline progress notes required. Reconciled single delivery at end.

## Tools Used

- `list-workbook-datasources` — Phase 0 (identify target DS; multi-source ambiguity fires HC#1 clarifier).
- `list-available-fields` — Phase 1 (enumerate every calc; verbosity full to capture formula, type, AGG-flag, references). Locked threshold: batch calls in ~10-field groups with inline progress notes whenever the data sources field count exceeds 30. Below 30, single call.
- `resolve-field` — Phase 2 (resolve derivation prefix per calcs actual AGG-flag; never string-match the formula).
- `get-workbook-inventory` — Phase 3 (dashboard references only; it returns worksheet↔datasource associations, not per-field shelf placement).
- `search-workbook-fields` — Phase 3 (shelf placements: returns explicit Rows/Columns/Marks placement per field across worksheets). Optional. If either tool is unavailable, note `usage.unavailable_this_run: true` for the affected sub-field and proceed.
- No file writes. Skill is compute-only; downstream consumers write if desired.

## Catalog Schema (Locked, Per-Calc Entry)

Full schema in `skill-expertise/catalog_schema.md`. Summary of required fields per calc:

- **Identity:** `calc_name`, `calc_type` (row_level / aggregate / lod_fixed / lod_include / lod_exclude / table_calc), `formula`, `return_type`.
- **Reference graph:** `references.fields`, `references.parameters` (cited), `references.sets` (cited), `references.hierarchies` (cited), `references.nested_calcs`.
- **Style/perf/complexity flags:** `style_violations` (list of S-* rule IDs from calc-linters catalog, with severity), `perf_advisory_flags` (list of PA-* flags from calc-optimizers catalog), `complexity` (`line_count`, `branch_depth`, `nested_lod_depth`).
- **Usage:** `usage.shelf_placements` (count, from `search-workbook-fields`), `usage.dashboards` (list of dashboard names, from `get-workbook-inventory`), `usage.flag` (`unused` / `low_usage` / `in_use`).

Every catalog entry has all required fields populated. Missing values sentinel to `null`, `[]`, or `unavailable_this_run` per HC#8. Never blank.

## Phase Sequence

- **Phase 0.** Identify target data source. Multi-source ambiguity fires HC#1 clarifier.
- **Phase 1.** Enumerate every calc via `list-available-fields` (verbosity: full). Batch in ~10-field groups with inline progress notes. Record name, formula, type, AGG-flag, and raw reference list per calc.
- **Phase 2.** Resolve derivation prefix per calc via `resolve-field`. Classify `calc_type` and `return_type`. Build the reference graph across the whole inventory (nested-calc references, parameters, sets, hierarchies).
- **Phase 3.** Fetch dashboard references via `get-workbook-inventory` and shelf-placement counts via `search-workbook-fields`. Derive `usage.flag` from both. If either tool is unavailable, mark `usage.unavailable_this_run: true` and proceed.
- **Phase 4.** Apply flag heuristics: run each calc through `skill-expertise/style_catalog.md` and `skill-expertise/performance_hierarchy.md` (read-only reference; never extend). Record `style_violations` and `perf_advisory_flags` per calc.
- **Phase 5.** Compute `complexity` per calc (line count, branch depth, nested LOD depth) from the formula text.
- **Phase 6.** Reconcile batched results into a single deduplicated inventory. Run the 3-check V-gate (all fields populated, batches reconciled, reference-graph consistent).
- **Phase 7.** Render markdown table (scannable). Emit `calc_inventory_handoff/1` YAML unprompted.
- **Phase 8.** No cleanup needed (read-only; no scratch state).

## Validation Gate (Read-Only, 3 Checks)

Full spec in `skill-expertise/validation_gate.md`. Every inventory passes:

- **V1 (Entry completeness):** every catalog entry has all required schema fields populated (or sentinel values per HC#8). No blanks. No fabricated fields.
- **V2 (Batch reconciliation):** batched pagination results reconciled into a single inventory with zero duplicates and zero omissions. Verified by cross-checking total count against `list-available-fields`s reported count.
- **V3 (Reference-graph consistency):** every nested-calc reference in the inventory resolves to another entry in the inventory OR is flagged as `external_reference: true` with rationale. No dangling references. No cycles undetected (report cycles as `notes` on the affected calcs).

Any V-gate failure blocks delivery per HC#8. Fail-open is NOT applied here — since the skill is read-only, a V-gate failure means the inventory itself is incomplete or inconsistent, not a mutation risk. Refuse delivery and diagnose.

## Verification Derivation-Prefix Rule

Resolve derivation prefixes from each calcs actual AGG-flag via `list-available-fields`/`resolve-field`, not by string-matching the formula. Preserves the runtime-lookup discipline confirmed across the calc-family portfolio.

## Domain-Accuracy Assertions (Locked)

- Calc dependency graphs can have cycles (Calc A → Calc B → Calc A). Detect and report; do not attempt to break.
- A calcs `isAggregated` flag is authoritative for AGG classification; the formulas leading token is not. A `{FIXED ...}` LOD is AGG-flagged true even though the formula starts with `{`.
- A calc with zero downstream calc references AND zero shelf placements is unused — but not necessarily deletable; users may reference it via parameters or from other data sources.
- Parameters, sets, and hierarchies are cited by name, not resolved. calc-inventory does not follow references into those object types.
- Batched pagination MUST preserve calc identity across batches. Deduplicate on `calc_name` within a single data source (calc names are unique within a data source per Tableaus own model).

## Scale-Tier Branching

| Calc count | Handling |
|---|---|
| 0 | Empty inventory verdict, handoff with `total_count: 0`. |
| 1-19 | Single-pass enumeration. No batching. |
| 20-99 | Batched pagination in groups of ~20 with inline progress notes. |
| 100+ | Batched pagination + secondary batching of `list-available-fields` calls in ~10-field groups. Inline progress notes on both levels. Handoff `notes` documents both batching methods. |

## Bulk-Action Refusal Discipline (Locked)

calc-inventory catalogs; it does not act. Every bulk-action ask routes to the appropriate peer one calc at a time:

- Bulk-fix all style violations → calc-linter, one calc at a time (with HC#1 sequential-mode opt-in on the linter side).
- Bulk-optimize all tier-5 perf calcs → calc-optimizer, one calc at a time.
- Bulk-debug all NULL-returning calcs → calc-debugger, one calc at a time.
- Delete all unused calcs → refuse. No calc-delete tool exists on this platform; deletion is a manual Desktop step. Note in handoff.
- Rewrite every long-named calc → calc-linter with HC#12 overwrite-discipline gating per calc; never a single bulk pass.

## Report Structure (Locked)

Every inventory delivery renders this exact structure, even for empty inventory verdicts:

- **Summary:** N calcs cataloged, X unused, Y with style violations, Z with perf-advisory flags. Or Empty inventory — no calcs in this data source.
- **Markdown table:** one row per calc. Columns: `Name`, `Type`, `Formula (truncated)`, `References`, `Flags`, `Usage`. Wide tables paginate with clear break points.
- **Unused-calc list** (if any): explicit list of calcs with `usage.flag: unused`. Cleanup candidates.
- **Cycle report** (if any): any nested-calc cycles detected. Not automatically resolved (calc-inventory does not act).
- **`calc_inventory_handoff/1` YAML** with full structured data for downstream consumption.

## Handoff Contract

Emits `calc_inventory_handoff/1` unprompted after every delivery, including empty inventory verdicts. Full schema in `skill-expertise/handoff_schema.md`. Required non-blank fields:

- `schema_version`, `datasource_name`, `total_count`, `calcs` (list of catalog entries; may be empty for empty-inventory verdicts)
- `unused_calcs` (list of calc names; may be empty)
- `cycle_report` (list of detected cycles; may be empty)
- `batching_method` (`single_pass` / `paginated_20` / `paginated_20_plus_field_batching`)
- `usage_metadata_available` (true/false; based on `get-workbook-inventory` availability this run)

## Refuse to Fabricate

Never invent a calc entry. Never invent a rule ID outside calc-linters or calc-optimizers locked catalogs. Never estimate usage without live `get-workbook-inventory` data. Never act on calcs (no author, no edit, no delete). Never mark a calc as unused without confirming zero shelf placements AND zero downstream calc references.

## Graceful Degradation

These rules apply whenever something this skill needs is missing or fails. More specific rules elsewhere in this file take precedence.

- **Nothing to work on.** If no workbook is open, there is no data source, or the named calc, sheet, dashboard, or data source isn't found, stop before any other step. Say what you found (list the real names, if any) and ask the user to open the workbook or pick one. Never work on a guessed or closest-match target.
- **Tool call fails, times out, or returns empty.** Retry once, then stop retrying. Mark everything that depended on that call as not checked, continue with what you still can, and say which step failed. If the failed call was a write, stop and report the workbook's current state instead of continuing.
- **Partial results.** If any check, sheet, field, or data source wasn't evaluated, the summary says so (Partial: N of M checked; not checked: [list]). Never give a clean, ready, or PASS verdict on a partial run.
- **Reference file won't open.** Use the rules summarized in this file, say [file] unavailable; using the built-in summary, and never make up thresholds, rule IDs, or Desktop menu steps from memory.
- **Peer skill not installed.** If this skill would hand off to another skill that isn't available, say so and give the manual Desktop step instead. A handoff is never the only next step.
- **Platform gap.** If no tool can do something, say so plainly and give the manual Desktop path.
- **Failure messages.** Tell the user in plain language what was done, what wasn't, and the next step. No raw errors, stack traces, or JSON.
- **No fabrication.** Never invent fields, values, findings, or results to fill a gap left by a failed read.
