# Calc Migrator Diff Report — SKILL.md

Source: https://tableau.github.io/tableau-ai-utilities/tableau-studio-skills/tableau-agent/calc-family/calc-migrator-diff-report/SKILL

# Calc Migrator Diff Report

## When to use (full trigger detail)

Produce a per-calc source-DS vs. target-DS formula diff report from a calc-migrator run. Consumes calc_migration_report/1 handoff and re-validates each calc against current workbook state via V5 formula-hash and workbook fingerprint per portfolio-wide HC#15. For every migrated calc. source formula, target formula, field remaps applied, sentinels emitted, validation status, downstream routing signals. Read-only. Two-tier delivery. compact Tier A chat summary with top 5 findings plus opt-in Tier B full per-calc detail file save as .md or .txt per HC#11. Trigger with calc migration diff, diff my migration, review migration output, calc-migrator-diff-report, show migration changes, per calc migration diff. Do NOT trigger on. running a migration itself (route to calc-migrator), general hygiene audit (route to calc-hygiene-scan), rewriting migrated calcs (route to calc-writer or calc-optimizer), diagnosing NULL returns post-migration (route to calc-debugger), or workbook-level summary handoff (route to workbook-summary-onepager).

## Purpose

Produce a per-calc source-DS vs. target-DS formula diff report from a `calc-migrator` run. Consumes `calc_migration_report/1` handoff and re-validates each calc against current workbook state per portfolio-wide HC#15 staleness detection. Read-only. Every finding cites source formula, target formula, field remaps applied during migration, sentinels emitted, validation status, and downstream routing signal (calc-migrator re-run for unresolved, calc-writer for sentinels, calc-debugger for validation failures).

## Trigger Conditions

- calc migration diff
- diff my migration
- review migration output
- calc-migrator-diff-report
- show migration changes
- per calc migration diff
- what did the migration change
- audit my migration

## Do NOT Trigger On

- Running a migration itself → route to `calc-migrator`.
- General calc hygiene audit → route to `calc-hygiene-scan`.
- Rewriting migrated calcs to be simpler or faster → route to `calc-writer` or `calc-optimizer`.
- Diagnosing NULL returns post-migration → route to `calc-debugger`.
- Workbook-level summary handoff for stakeholders → route to `workbook-summary-onepager`.
- Explaining a single migrated calc in plain language → route to `calc-explainer`.
- Documenting every calc in detail (full dictionary) → route to `calc-documenter`.

## Scope Boundaries

- **IN.** One migration run per invocation. Read-only. Per-calc source-DS vs. target-DS formula diff. Required `calc_migration_report/1` handoff consumption with V5 formula-hash per-calc + workbook-fingerprint staleness detection per HC#15. Field-remap surfacing per calc. Sentinel surfacing per calc (whatever calc-migrator emitted as `unable to determine` gets its own diff-report finding). Validation-status surfacing per calc. Bulk-migration handling per HC#16 (50+ calcs). Downstream routing signals per finding. Handoff schema `calc_migration_diff/1`. Two-tier delivery: compact Tier A chat + opt-in Tier B file save as `.md` or `.txt`.
- **OUT.** Any workbook mutation. Running the migration itself (route to calc-migrator). Rewriting migrated calcs (route to calc-writer / calc-optimizer). NULL-return diagnosis (route to calc-debugger). Multi-migration-run comparison (single-migration-run diff only). PDF or DOCX output (`.md` and `.txt` only). Diff against prior migration runs.

## The Per-Calc Diff Schema (Locked)

Every diff finding cites a `finding_type`. Multi-type findings tier by highest severity. Full detection criteria, evidence patterns, and worked examples in `skill-expertise/diff_catalog.md`.

| # | Finding Type | ID | Severity | Signal source | Downstream routing |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Clean migration (formula changed, all fields remapped, validated) | DIFF-CLEAN-01 | Info | handoff + re-validation | None (no action needed) |
| 2 | Field-remap applied | DIFF-REMAP-02 | Info | handoff `field_remaps[]` | None (informational) |
| 3 | Sentinel emitted by calc-migrator (unresolved field, unresolvable calc) | DIFF-SENTINEL-03 | Warning | handoff `sentinels[]` | calc-writer (manual authoring) |
| 4 | Validation failure post-migration (target formula fails syntax or type check) | DIFF-VALIDATION-04 | Warning | handoff `validation_status` + re-validation | calc-debugger (NULL / error diagnosis) |
| 5 | Staleness detected (source workbook state changed since migration ran) | DIFF-STALE-05 | Warning | V5 formula-hash mismatch per calc, workbook-fingerprint mismatch | calc-migrator (re-run) |
| 6 | Unmigrated calc (in source but not in migration report) | DIFF-UNMIGRATED-06 | Warning | source-DS calc list vs. handoff `migrated_calcs[]` | calc-migrator (re-run with wider scope) |
| 7 | Formula-identical migration (target formula byte-identical to source; no remap needed) | DIFF-IDENTICAL-07 | Info | handoff formula comparison | None (informational; may indicate no-op migration) |

**Multi-type tagging.** A calc can fire multiple finding types (e.g., DIFF-REMAP-02 + DIFF-VALIDATION-04 both fire when field remap applied but target formula still fails validation). Skill emits all triggered finding IDs in `findings_triggered[]`; severity tier set by highest match. Deterministic sort per HC#10: severity tier (Warning → Info) → finding ID ascending → calc name alphabetical.

**Fallback discipline (HC#5).** When diff detection depends on data thats unavailable per calc (handoff missing formula body, re-validation tool call fails), skill emits `unable to determine` sentinel per HC#5 for that specific finding type on that specific calc. Other finding types on the same calc still evaluate.

## Workflow Phases

- **Phase 0 Scope.** Confirm `calc_migration_report/1` handoff is available in session context. If missing, stop and tell the user to run `calc-migrator` first — do not proceed to Phase 1 on a missing handoff. Confirm workbook is open via `get-workbook-inventory`; if the call fails, returns no workbook, or the session is disconnected, stop and tell the user to confirm Tableau Studio is open with a workbook loaded. Ensure one migration run per invocation per HC#2.
- **Phase 1 Handoff Verification.** Verify `calc_migration_report/1` handoff completeness. Field mapping from calc-migrator's `calc_migration_report/1`: `source_datasource` = `source.datasource`; `target_datasource` = `target.datasource`; the single migrated calc is `migrated_calcs[0]` with `source_formula` = `source.formula`, `target_formula` = `target.formula`, `field_remaps[]` = `consent_log[]`, `sentinels[]` = `unresolved_references[]`, `validation_status` = `status` plus `v_gate`. Apply this mapping before checking completeness. Required fields: `source_datasource`, `target_datasource`, `migrated_calcs[]` with per-calc `source_formula`, `target_formula`, `field_remaps[]`, `sentinels[]`, `validation_status`. If any required field is missing on the handoff itself, treat the run as incomplete and emit `handoff_incomplete: true` in output metadata; skill can still render diff for the calcs that do have complete data, but flags the handoff as partial. Populate workbook-fingerprint from `get-workbook-inventory` for HC#15 comparison in Phase 2. **Single-fetch discipline:** `get-workbook-inventory` is called once in Phase 1; its result (workbook fingerprint and inventory snapshot) is cached and reused for both the Phase 1 completeness check and the Phase 2 staleness re-validation — never re-fetched mid-run.
- **Phase 2 Re-Validation (numbered checklist).**
  1. For each calc in `migrated_calcs[]`, verify V5 formula-hash on the target formula against current workbook state. `formula-hash` and `workbook fingerprint` are values computed by this skill (a hash of the formula text and a hash of overall workbook state), not native Tableau APIs or Tableau-exposed properties — they exist purely for this skills own staleness bookkeeping. If the target formulas formula-hash from the handoff does not match the current workbooks formula-hash for that calc name on the target datasource, mark the calc `stale: true` and fire DIFF-STALE-05.
  2. Verify workbook fingerprint from the handoff matches current workbook fingerprint per HC#15. If mismatch, mark the whole run `run_stale: true`; per-calc staleness still evaluated individually via step 1.
  3. Re-validate every calcs target formula against the target datasource. Batch `resolve-field` calls in groups of 20 per portfolio-wide HC batching cap (matches calc-migrators Phase 2 pattern). If a batch call fails outright (timeout, disconnect), retry that batch once; on a second failure, emit `unable to determine` sentinel for every calc dependent on that batchs resolution and continue with remaining batches — do not abort the whole diff.
  4. For each calc, apply the 7 finding types from `skill-expertise/diff_catalog.md`. Populate `findings_triggered[]` with the finding ID, evidence citation, and `signal_source`.
  5. Enumerate source-DS calc list via `list-available-fields` and compare to handoff `migrated_calcs[]`. Any source calc not in the handoff fires DIFF-UNMIGRATED-06.
  6. For findings with unresolvable signals, emit `unable to determine` sentinel per HC#5 rather than skipping.
- **Phase 3 Severity Tiering + Deterministic Sort.** Sort per HC#10: severity tier (Warning → Info) → finding ID ascending → calc name alphabetical. Warning-tier findings surface in Tier A top 5.
- **Phase 4 Validate.** Run the 5-check V-gate: finding coverage, per-calc signal-source attribution, ordering determinism, handoff completeness, downstream routing correctness. If any check fails, do not discard the run: re-run only the failing checks underlying data pull once (e.g., re-fetch signal-source labels for V2, re-sort for V3), then re-validate that check. If it fails a second time, deliver Tier A with the specific V-check named as unresolved and the affected calcs/findings listed, rather than blocking delivery entirely or silently passing.
- **Phase 5 Deliver.** Two-tier: compact Tier A chat summary with counts and top 5 Warning-tier findings (staleness, validation failures, sentinels, unmigrated calcs); opt-in Tier B file save requires user path confirmation per HC#11.

## Hard Constraints

**HC#1 Read-only always.** Never mutates the workbook. Never invokes calc-migrator to re-run. Every finding is a diagnostic; downstream routing signals emitted but skill never chains invocation.

**HC#2 One migration run per invocation.** Multi-migration-run comparison refused.

**HC#3 7-finding-type catalog locked.** No finding type omitted, no fabricated finding type added. Detection follows the criteria in `skill-expertise/diff_catalog.md`.

**HC#4 Refuse to fabricate.** No inferred field remaps, no guessed migration rationale, no invented validation results. Sentinels: `null`, `unable to determine`, empty-state prose.

**HC#5 Sentinel discipline per finding per calc.** When a findings detection fails on a specific calc (handoff missing formula body, re-validation tool call fails for that calc), emit `unable to determine` sentinel for that finding on that calc. Other findings on the same calc still evaluate; other calcs still get all 7 finding types.

**HC#6 Handoff data quoted verbatim.** Source formula, target formula, field remaps, and sentinels from calc-migrators handoff are quoted byte-identical. Skill supplements around handoff data; never rewrites or paraphrases the migration output.

**HC#7 Sentinel discipline for zero-calc migration.** If handoff `migrated_calcs[]` is empty, exit cleanly with no calcs migrated in this run; diff report not applicable. Zero-calc source datasource also exits cleanly.

**HC#8 Diff-mode transparency** (portfolio-wide HC#13). Repeat invocations against unchanged handoff state emit `diff_mode: reused_verbatim` in Tier A. Fresh-scan / reused-verbatim / targeted-rescan enum. Note: `diff_mode` here refers to the diff-reports own idempotency, not to the migration diff content itself — the report is always presenting migration-diff content, but `diff_mode` tracks whether this specific report invocation is a fresh render or a re-render of unchanged inputs.

**HC#9 Ordering determinism** (portfolio-wide HC#14). Sort key locked: severity tier → finding ID → calc name alphabetical. Same input produces byte-identical top-5 and full findings list across runs.

**HC#10 Handoff-or-revalidation labeled per finding.** Every finding records `signal_source: handoff | revalidation | handoff+revalidation | unresolved` so downstream consumers know evidence origin. `handoff` = pure handoff data (e.g., field remap surfacing); `revalidation` = current-state re-check (e.g., staleness detection); `handoff+revalidation` = combines both (e.g., validation failure confirmed against current state).

**HC#11 Never silent file write.** Tier B save requires user path confirmation AND format choice (`.md` or `.txt`). No default writes to Downloads.

**HC#12 Downstream routing signals, never routing invocation.** For each Warning-tier finding, emit routing signals: DIFF-SENTINEL-03 → `routing.calc_writer: true`, DIFF-VALIDATION-04 → `routing.calc_debugger: true`, DIFF-STALE-05 and DIFF-UNMIGRATED-06 → `routing.calc_migrator: true`. Skill never invokes downstream skills directly per HC#1; user opts in.

**HC#13 Handoff staleness detection required** (portfolio-wide HC#15). V5 formula-hash check per calc when consuming calc-migration handoff. Per-calc mismatch fires DIFF-STALE-05 for that specific calc; other calcs with fresh hash-match still render normally. Workbook-fingerprint check per HC#15 fires run-level staleness.

**HC#14 Reference-file grounding.** All 7 finding types cite detection criteria and worked examples in `skill-expertise/diff_catalog.md`. Threshold defenses (V5 formula-hash discipline, validation-status semantics from calc-migrator, source-vs-target formula comparison rules) all documented with cross-references to calc-migrators contract.

**HC#15 Wide-workbook / bulk-migration scale handling.** For migration runs with 50+ calcs, skill emits a bulk-migration-notice in Tier A (this migration touched N calcs; Tier A truncates to top 5 per severity tier, full findings list in Tier B). Per-calc evaluation still runs on every calc; only presentation truncates. Warning-tier findings always surface fully in Tier A even beyond 5 if all are Warning; only Info-tier truncates. Per-calc evaluation cost scales linearly with calc count — there is no upper bound on migration size beyond the resolve-field groups-of-20 batching cap in Phase 2 step 3; a 200-calc migration runs the same per-calc logic as a 5-calc one, just in more batches.

**HC#16 Handoff completeness check.** Required fields on `calc_migration_report/1`: `source_datasource`, `target_datasource`, `migrated_calcs[]` (each with `source_formula`, `target_formula`, `field_remaps[]`, `sentinels[]`, `validation_status`). If handoff is missing any required field on the run-level, refuse with a route to re-run calc-migrator. If handoff is present but a specific calcs fields are incomplete, emit sentinels for those calcs per HC#5 and continue rendering the others. `resolve-field` case-sensitivity concern (a known platform gap, shared with calc-family): re-validation uses exact-case matches per HC#5 fallback.

## Validation Gate (5-Check)

- **V1 Finding Coverage.** All 7 finding types evaluated against every migrated calc plus any unmigrated source calcs.
- **V2 Signal-Source Attribution.** Every finding has `signal_source` populated per HC#10.
- **V3 Ordering Determinism.** Findings sort key deterministic per HC#9.
- **V4 Handoff Completeness.** `handoff_verified`, `handoff_incomplete`, `run_stale`, and per-calc `stale` flags all populated. Workbook-fingerprint match verified.
- **V5 Downstream Routing Correctness.** Every Warning-tier finding has the correct `routing.*` flag set per HC#12 (SENTINEL-03 → calc_writer, VALIDATION-04 → calc_debugger, STALE-05 / UNMIGRATED-06 → calc_migrator).

## Two-Tier Delivery

**Tier A (chat).** Compact summary: source datasource, target datasource, calcs migrated, findings by severity tier, top 5 Warning-tier findings with per-calc detail and downstream routing signals where applicable.

Template:

```
**Calc Migration Diff Report: {source_ds} → {target_ds}**
Calcs migrated: {N}
Findings: {N_warning} Warning, {N_info} Info, {N_sentinel} sentinel
Handoff verified: {yes/no}, run stale: {yes/no}
Diff mode: {fresh_scan | reused_verbatim | targeted_rescan}

Top 5 Warning-tier findings:
1. [{calc_name}] {finding_id}: {evidence}. Source: `{source_formula}`. Target: `{target_formula}`. Routing: {calc_migrator | calc_writer | calc_debugger}.
2. ...

Routing offered: calc-migrator (for stale / unmigrated), calc-writer (for sentinels), calc-debugger (for validation failures).
Save full diff report to file? (.md or .txt)
```

**Tier B (opt-in file save).** Full report `.md` (default) or `.txt` written to user-confirmed path per HC#11. Unbounded length. Per-calc detail: source formula, target formula, field-remap list, sentinels emitted, validation status, staleness status, downstream routing flags. Handoff YAML block appended.

## Handoff Schema

Emits `calc_migration_diff/1`. Downstream: `calc-migrator` (re-run for STALE-05 / UNMIGRATED-06), `calc-writer` (manual authoring for SENTINEL-03), `calc-debugger` (NULL / error diagnosis for VALIDATION-04), `workbook-auditor` (migration-diff delta tracking).

Fields include: source_datasource, target_datasource, run_timestamp (from calc-migrator handoff), diff_mode, handoff_verified, handoff_incomplete, run_stale, workbook_fingerprint_current, workbook_fingerprint_migration, calcs[] with per-calc findings_triggered / signal_source / stale / routing, totals (warning_count, info_count, sentinel_count, unmigrated_count), routing_offered (calc_migrator, calc_writer, calc_debugger, workbook_auditor), v_gate results.

## Common Mistakes (Anti-Patterns)

- **Auto-invoking calc-migrator to re-run.** HC#1 read-only + HC#12 routing-only. Skill emits `routing.calc_migrator: true` on STALE-05 / UNMIGRATED-06; user opts in.
- **Silent stale-handoff rendering.** HC#13 requires per-calc V5 formula-hash check plus run-level workbook-fingerprint check. Stale-per-calc fires DIFF-STALE-05; stale-per-run marks the whole run.
- **Rewriting handoff data.** HC#6 quotes source/target formulas verbatim. Skill supplements around them; never paraphrases.
- **Fabricating field remaps.** HC#4. DIFF-REMAP-02 evidence comes from handoff `field_remaps[]`; no inferred remaps.
- **Missing DIFF-UNMIGRATED-06 coverage.** HC#3 + V1 require enumerating source-DS calc list and comparing to handoff `migrated_calcs[]`. Source calcs absent from handoff fire this finding.
- **Silent file write on Tier B save.** HC#11 requires path confirmation AND format choice (`.md` or `.txt`).
- **Skipping a finding on a specific calc.** HC#5 requires all 7 finding types evaluated per calc (where applicable), with sentinel for unresolvable signals.
- **Confusing diff-mode enum with diff content.** HC#8 clarifies: `diff_mode` tracks this skills own idempotency across re-invocations; the migration-diff content itself is always the same 7-finding-type report.

## Adjacent-Skill Routing

- **Upstream required:** `calc-migrator` (produces `calc_migration_report/1` handoff).
- **Downstream opt-in per finding:**
  - DIFF-SENTINEL-03 → `calc-writer` (manual authoring for calcs calc-migrator couldnt resolve).
  - DIFF-VALIDATION-04 → `calc-debugger` (NULL / error diagnosis for target formula that fails validation).
  - DIFF-STALE-05 → `calc-migrator` (re-run because workbook state changed since migration).
  - DIFF-UNMIGRATED-06 → `calc-migrator` (re-run with wider scope to catch missed source calcs).
- **Downstream general:** `workbook-auditor` for migration-diff delta across runs.
- **Refusal routes:** running migration → `calc-migrator`; hygiene audit → `calc-hygiene-scan`; rewriting migrated calcs → `calc-writer` / `calc-optimizer`; NULL diagnosis → `calc-debugger`; workbook-level summary → `workbook-summary-onepager`; single-calc explanation → `calc-explainer`; full documentation → `calc-documenter`.

## Known Limitations

- Supports `.md` and `.txt` only.
- **DIFF-VALIDATION-04 depends on calc-migrators `validation_status` field being populated.** If calc-migrator emitted the field but with a coarse-grained value (e.g., `passed` / `failed` without per-check breakdown), diff-report inherits that granularity and cannot decompose further.
- **DIFF-UNMIGRATED-06 relies on complete source-DS calc enumeration via `list-available-fields`.** If that tool returns incomplete calc lists on a specific datasource, DIFF-UNMIGRATED-06 may miss calcs that should have fired it. HC#5 sentinel discipline applies.
- **`resolve-field` case-sensitivity concern**. Re-validation uses handoff data preferentially; local-extract fallback exact-case matches per rule.
- **Bulk-migration Tier A cap at top 5 per severity may hide Info-tier detail.** By design: Warning-tier always surfaces fully; Info-tier truncates. Full Info detail in Tier B.

## Graceful Degradation

These rules apply whenever something this skill needs is missing or fails. More specific rules elsewhere in this file take precedence.

- **Nothing to work on.** If no workbook is open, there is no data source, or the named calc, sheet, dashboard, or data source isn't found, stop before any other step. Say what you found (list the real names, if any) and ask the user to open the workbook or pick one. Never work on a guessed or closest-match target.
- **Tool call fails, times out, or returns empty.** Retry once, then stop retrying. Mark everything that depended on that call as not checked, continue with what you still can, and say which step failed. If the failed call was a write, stop and report the workbook's current state instead of continuing.
- **Partial results.** If any check, sheet, field, or data source wasn't evaluated, the summary says so (Partial: N of M checked; not checked: [list]). Never give a clean, ready, or PASS verdict on a partial run.
- **Reference file won't open.** Use the rules summarized in this file, say [file] unavailable; using the built-in summary, and never make up thresholds, rule IDs, or Desktop menu steps from memory.
- **Peer skill not installed.** If this skill would hand off to another skill that isn't available, say so and give the manual Desktop step instead. A handoff is never the only next step.
- **Platform gap.** If no tool can do something, say so plainly and give the manual Desktop path.
- **Failure messages.** Tell the user in plain language what was done, what wasn't, and the next step. No raw errors, stack traces, or JSON.
- **No fabrication.** Never invent fields, values, findings, or results to fill a gap left by a failed read.

# Calc Documenter — when to use

Source: https://tableau.github.io/tableau-ai-utilities/tableau-studio-skills/tableau-agent/calc-family/calc-documenter

## What it does

Scans every calculated field in an open Tableau workbook and produces a five-dimension dictionary entry per calc: formula (verbatim), fields referenced, reference graph (uses and used-by), sheet / dashboard usage, and aggregation context (row-level, aggregate, LOD-fixed, LOD-include, LOD-exclude, or table-calc). Author captions and in-formula `//` comments are preserved verbatim. Read-only. Nothing gets written back to the workbook. Chat delivers a compact summary; the full dictionary saves to a file only if you confirm the path.

## When to use it

- "I inherited a workbook with 40 calcs and I need to understand what's there before I touch it"
- "I need to hand this workbook off and want a proper calc dictionary as part of the handoff"
- "I want to see the reference graph so I know which calcs get consumed by other calcs vs. dead ends"
- "I need to run this before calc-explainer or calc-linter so the downstream skills have a handoff to consume"
- "I want to catch circular calc references or unused calcs during a governance sweep"

## When NOT to use it

- Not for explaining a single calc in plain language (use `calc-explainer`)
- Not for diagnosing why a calc returns NULL (use `calc-debugger`)
- Not for calc naming, hygiene, or comment audit (use `calc-linter`)
- Not for calc performance rewrites (use `calc-optimizer`)
- Not for authoring new calcs (use `calc-writer`)
- Not for cross-workbook or multi-workbook bulk runs (one workbook per invocation)

## How to trigger it

- "document all calcs in this workbook"
- "generate a calc dictionary"
- "calc-documenter"
- "produce a calc reference for this workbook"
- "build a dependency graph of the calcs"

# Calc Documenter — SKILL.md

Source: https://tableau.github.io/tableau-ai-utilities/tableau-studio-skills/tableau-agent/calc-family/calc-documenter/SKILL

# Calc Documenter

## When to use (full trigger detail)

Generate structural documentation for every calculated field in a Tableau workbook. Emits a per-calc dictionary with formula, fields referenced, reference graph (uses / used-by), sheets and dashboards using the calc, inferred aggregation level (row-level / aggregate / LOD fixed-include-exclude), and any existing author caption preserved verbatim. Read-only. Trigger with document my calcs, generate calc docs, calc dictionary, reference graph for calcs, calc-documenter, which calcs do I have, map my calc dependencies. Do NOT trigger on. single-calc explanation (defer to calc-explainer), calc syntax debugging (defer to calc-debugger), calc-family hygiene or naming audit (defer to calc-linter), applying documentation changes to calc captions (this skill is read-only), performance optimization (defer to calc-optimizer), workbook change-over-time (defer to workbook-auditor).

## Purpose

Generate structural documentation for every calculated field in a Tableau workbook. Emits a per-calc dictionary sorted by dependency order (or alphabetical fallback) with formula, referenced fields, reference graph, sheet/dashboard usage, inferred aggregation context, and preserved author captions. Read-only. Every entry cites XML evidence; no fabrication.

Positioned parallel to calc-inventory in the calc-family pipeline. Calc-inventory discovers what calcs exist; calc-documenter documents what each one is, does, and connects to. Downstream skills (calc-explainer, workbook-auditor, publish-readiness) consume the handoff.

## Trigger Conditions

- document my calcs
- generate calc docs
- calc dictionary
- reference graph for calcs
- calc-documenter
- which calcs do I have
- map my calc dependencies
- who uses this calc

## Do NOT Trigger On

- Single-calc natural-language explanation (defer to `calc-explainer`).
- Calc syntax debugging or NULL diagnosis (defer to `calc-debugger`).
- Calc-family hygiene, naming, or commenting audit (defer to `calc-linter`).
- Rewriting or applying documentation changes (all fixes are Desktop-manual per HC#1).
- Performance optimization (defer to `calc-optimizer`).
- Change-over-time (defer to `workbook-auditor`).
- Data-quality issues (defer to `data-quality-review`).
- Chart-type advisory (defer to `chart-swap-advisor`).
- Format-string drift (defer to `format-drift-scanner`).

## Scope Boundaries

- **IN.** One workbook per run. Every calculated field across every datasource in the workbook. Formula extracted verbatim from XML. Fields referenced (measures, dimensions, parameters, other calcs) parsed from formula and cross-referenced against `list-available-fields`. Reference graph (uses / used-by) constructed across the calc family. Sheets and dashboards pinning each calc to a shelf. Inferred aggregation context (row-level, aggregate, LOD fixed-include-exclude). Author captions preserved verbatim. Read-only. Handoff schema `calc_documentation/1`.
- **OUT.** Any workbook mutation. Applying doc changes to calc captions. Explaining a specific calc in plain language (calc-explainer). Naming or hygiene audit (calc-linter). Performance analysis. Multi-workbook runs.

**Cross-datasource workbooks.** Each datasources calcs documented in its own section. Cross-datasource references (calc in DS-A referring to a field in DS-B) flagged in the doc entry as `cross_datasource_reference`.

## The 5-Dimension Documentation Model

Every calc gets these five documentation dimensions:

| Dimension | Source | Verbatim? |
|---|---|---|
| Formula | `list-available-fields` `formula` attribute, with internal `Calculation_NNNN...` field-name tokens swapped for their resolved caption/name (see HC#16) | Yes, modulo caption substitution |
| Fields referenced | Parsed from formula, resolved via `resolve-field` | List, deduplicated |
| Reference graph | Cross-computed from every calcs Fields Referenced list | Directed (uses → used-by) |
| Sheet/dashboard usage | `get-worksheet-xml` shelves + `get-dashboard-xml` filters/parameters | List by name |
| Aggregation context | Inferred from formula (SUM/AVG/COUNT → aggregate; FIXED/INCLUDE/EXCLUDE → LOD-typed; no aggregate → row-level) | Enum |
| Author caption | XML `caption` attribute or worksheet-scoped description | Preserved verbatim |

**Sixth dimension (optional).** If a `<comment>` or annotation exists in the XML attached to the calc, include as `author_annotation`. Rare in most workbooks.

## Workflow Phases

- **Phase 0 Scope.** Confirm workbook is open via `get-workbook-inventory`. Enumerate datasources via `list-workbook-datasources`. For each datasource, enumerate calcs via `list-available-fields` filtered to calc-type fields. Ask user to scope only if total calc count exceeds 100 (default: all).
- **Phase 1 Extract.** For each calc: read formula, caption, aggregation attribute from XML. Parse formula for field references. Resolve each reference via `resolve-field` (batched per HC#5). Extract sheet/dashboard usage via `get-worksheet-xml` and `get-dashboard-xml`.
- **Phase 2 Build Reference Graph.** For every pair of calcs (A, B), if As formula references B, record A → B (uses) and B → A (used-by). Detect cycles; flag any circular dependency as `CD-CYCLE-01`.
- **Phase 3 Infer Aggregation Context.** For each calc, classify as row-level, aggregate, or LOD-fixed/LOD-include/LOD-exclude via formula pattern match. Cite the pattern that fired the classification.
- **Phase 4 Assemble Dictionary.** Sort calcs by dependency order (least-referenced first), fall back to alphabetical on ties. Group by datasource. Emit per-calc entries per `skill-expertise/documentation_template.md`.
- **Phase 5 Deliver Tier A.** Compact chat summary: total calc count, dependency-graph shape (linear, tree, DAG, cyclic), top 3 most-referenced calcs, save-file offer.
- **Phase 6 Deliver Tier B (opt-in).** Full dictionary written to Downloads as `.md` (default) or `.txt` only after user confirms path.

## Hard Constraints

**HC#1 Read-only always.** Never invoke `author-calc`, `bind-template`, `build-and-apply-worksheet`, or any mutating tool. Documentation is emitted; nothing is written back to the workbook.

**HC#2 One workbook per run.** Multi-workbook doc runs refused. Users invoke separately.

**HC#3 Bulk-action refusal.** Document all calcs and apply captions refused; skill is read-only per HC#1.

**HC#4 Locked five-dimension model.** Every calc entry includes formula, fields referenced, reference graph position, sheet/dashboard usage, aggregation context, and (if present) author caption. No dimension omitted. No fabricated dimension added.

**HC#5 Batching cap.** `resolve-field` batches capped at 20 per parallel call; `get-worksheet-xml` batches capped at 10 sheets per parallel call. Sequence remaining sheets in additional batches.

**HC#6 Never auto-invoke another skill.** Adjacent-skill routing (calc-explainer for natural-language explanation, calc-linter for hygiene) is an opt-in handoff.

**HC#7 Sentinel discipline.** Use `null`, `[]`, `unresolved` for missing XML fields. Never blank fields in the handoff schema. Field references that cannot be resolved via `resolve-field` render as `unresolved: <raw_reference>` in the doc entry.

**HC#8 Refuse to fabricate.** V-gate refuses fabricated field references, invented aggregation classifications, or missing formula citations.

**HC#9 Partial-info handling.** If `list-available-fields` returns partial results (per a known reliability gap), flag `PARTIAL-EXTRACT` for that datasource with reason; do not proceed with incomplete evidence.

**HC#10 Adjacent-skill routing.** Natural-language explanation → `calc-explainer`. Hygiene audit → `calc-linter`. Debugging → `calc-debugger`. Optimization → `calc-optimizer`.

**HC#11 Author caption preserved verbatim.** If the calc has an existing caption, description, or annotation in XML, include it in the entry as `author_description` or `author_annotation` verbatim. Never rewrite, paraphrase, or omit. Author intent is preserved even if it conflicts with the skills structural doc.

**HC#12 Never write the longform file silently.** File-save requires explicit user opt-in with path confirmation. Full dictionary lives in the file only; chat renders summary + top 3 only.

**HC#13 Guide the user actively.** Silence during evaluation is a defect. Announce progress on 50+ calc runs (per-datasource progress markers).

**HC#14 Cycle detection required.** Reference-graph construction detects and flags circular dependencies as `CD-CYCLE-01`. Never rendered as a valid dependency graph; cycles are flagged and the affected calcs marked `in_cycle: true`.

**HC#15 Ordering locked.** Dictionary entries render in dependency order (topological sort, least-referenced first). Alphabetical on ties. Within-datasource sort only; datasources render in `list-workbook-datasources` enumeration order.

**HC#16 Formula display must use resolved captions, not internal field IDs.** `list-available-fields` returns raw formula text containing internal tokens like `[Calculation_0831103151444568]` wherever the formula references another calc by its underlying column name rather than its caption. Before rendering a Formula line, every such token MUST be substituted with the referenced calc's resolved caption/name (e.g. `[Calculation_0831103151444568]` → `[Days to Ship Actual]`), using the same `resolve-field` lookups already performed for Fields Referenced in Phase 1. If a token cannot be resolved, leave it as the raw internal ID and flag it `"unresolved: <raw_token>"` per HC#7 — never silently display an unresolved internal ID as if it were final. When substitution occurs, append one line directly under the Formula block: `(stored internally as [<raw_token>, ...]; captions shown above)` so the reader knows the formula was translated, not misquoted. This check is part of V2 (Formula Citation) and blocks delivery on failure per HC#8.

## Two-Tier Delivery

### Tier A: Compact chat summary (always renders)

Target under 25 lines.

```
**Calc Documentation: {workbook_name}**
Datasources: {N} · Total calcs: {N} · Graph shape: {linear | tree | DAG | cyclic}
{Cycle banner if CD-CYCLE-01 fired, one line}

Per-datasource TL;DR:
- {DS-A}: {N} calcs, {N} row-level, {N} aggregate, {N} LOD, {N} with author captions
- {DS-B}: same shape

Top 3 most-referenced calcs (used-by count):
1. {calc_name}: used by {N} other calcs, on {M} sheets
2. {calc_name}: used by {N}, on {M}
3. {calc_name}: used by {N}, on {M}

Save the full dictionary to Downloads? (.md default, .txt option, or skip)
```

### Tier B: Full dictionary file (opt-in)

Path: `{Downloads}/{workbook_name}_calc-documentation.md` (or `.txt`). Fresh-filename discipline on collision.

Contents per `skill-expertise/documentation_template.md`:

- Header (skill version, timestamp, workbook name, calc count, graph shape).
- Cycle warnings section (if any CD-CYCLE-01 fired).
- Per-datasource sections with per-calc entries in dependency order:
  - Name and caption (author caption verbatim if present).
  - Formula (verbatim from XML, code-block formatted).
  - Fields referenced (list; resolved names).
  - Reference graph position: `Uses: [list]`, `Used by: [list]`.
  - Sheet/dashboard usage: `On sheets: [list]`, `On dashboards: [list]`.
  - Aggregation context: `Type: {row-level | aggregate | LOD-fixed | LOD-include | LOD-exclude}`. Pattern cited.
  - Cross-datasource references (if any).
  - Author annotation (if any XML `<comment>` attached).
- Handoff schema payload (`calc_documentation/1`) at the bottom.

**File-save discipline (HC#12).** User opts in, format confirmed, path confirmed OS-agnostically, fresh-filename discipline on collision.

## Validation Gate (4-Check Read-Only)

**V1 Dimension Coverage.** Every calc entry has all 5 required dimensions populated (formula, fields referenced, reference graph position, sheet/dashboard usage, aggregation context) or sentinel with reason.

**V2 Formula Citation.** Every field-reference cites the formula substring that mentioned it. No fabricated references. Formula display text contains no unresolved internal `Calculation_NNNN...` tokens where a caption resolution was available (HC#16); any token that genuinely could not be resolved is flagged, not silently shown raw.

**V3 Handoff Completeness.** Every field in `calc_documentation/1` populated per `skill-expertise/handoff_schema.md`.

**V4 Ordering + Cycle Discipline.** Entries render in dependency order (topological sort). Cycles flagged per HC#14. Author captions preserved per HC#11. Datasource enum order per HC#15.

V-gate failure blocks delivery per HC#8.

## Tool Sequence

- **Phase 0.** `get-workbook-inventory` (never twice per run). `list-workbook-datasources` for datasource enumeration. `list-available-fields` per datasource, filtered to calc fields.
- **Phase 1.** `resolve-field` per formula reference (batched, 20 per parallel call). `get-worksheet-xml` per worksheet with calcs on shelves (batched, 10 per parallel call). `get-dashboard-xml` per dashboard with calc-driven filters/parameters.
- **Phase 2-4.** In-memory reference-graph construction and dictionary assembly. No tool calls.
- **Phase 5.** Chat delivery. No tool calls.
- **Phase 6.** File-write to Downloads only on opt-in per HC#12.

**Batching rules.** Never call `get-workbook-inventory` twice per run. Never call `list-available-fields` twice per datasource. Batch `resolve-field` and `get-worksheet-xml` per HC#5. If a `get-worksheet-xml` batch call fails, retry the failed sheets individually rather than failing the whole batch — a single dashboard-bound sheet 500 (see Known Limitations) should not blank out usage data for the other sheets in that batch.

**Early-exit condition.** If `list-workbook-datasources` returns zero datasources (workbook not open or empty), exit with No datasources found; open a workbook with calculated fields to document.

## Handoff Contract

Emits `calc_documentation/1` per `skill-expertise/handoff_schema.md`. Consumed by:

- **calc-explainer.** Uses the reference graph to explain how a specific calc fits into the calc family.
- **calc-linter.** Uses author-caption presence to flag under-documented calcs.
- **calc-debugger.** Uses reference graph to trace NULL propagation across dependent calcs.
- **workbook-auditor.** Consumes documentation deltas across runs (calc added, removed, changed).
- **publish-readiness.** Verifies critical calcs are documented before publish.

## Known Limitations

- **`list-available-fields` reliability gap**. Some workbooks return partial calc lists. HC#9 flags PARTIAL-EXTRACT rather than fabricating.
- **Cross-datasource references.** Detected but not always resolvable if the target datasource isnt loaded. Rendered as `cross_datasource_reference: {ds_name}.{field_name}` without full resolution.
- **Table-calc computed context.** Table calcs (WINDOW_SUM, RUNNING_SUM, etc.) have partition/addressing configured on the worksheet, not in the calc XML. Aggregation context lists these as `table-calc`; specific addressing not documented per calc (defers to sheet-level docs).
- **Set / parameter references.** Documented as fields but the underlying set membership or parameter value list is not enumerated (thats set-audit and parameter-manager territory, both out of scope).
- **Author caption formatting.** Preserved verbatim including any markdown, line breaks, or special characters. No sanitization.
- **`get-worksheet-xml` reliability gap on dashboard-bound sheets.** Confirmed to intermittently 500 on populated worksheets already placed on a dashboard. When this fires for a given sheet, render that sheets `on_sheets`/`on_dashboards` contribution as `unresolved: xml-read-failed` per HC#7 sentinel discipline rather than omitting the dimension or silently rendering an incomplete usage list.

## Error Handling

| Failure | Response |
|---|---|
| Workbook not open | Ask: Please open the workbook youd like documented. |
| `get-workbook-inventory` fails | Retry once. If still failing, exit gracefully. |
| `list-workbook-datasources` returns empty | Exit with No datasources found; nothing to document. |
| `list-available-fields` returns partial | Flag PARTIAL-EXTRACT for that datasource per HC#9. |
| `resolve-field` returns no match for a formula reference | Render as `unresolved: <raw_reference>` in the entry per HC#7. |
| Circular calc dependency detected | Flag CD-CYCLE-01. Do not render a valid dependency chain. Mark affected calcs `in_cycle: true`. |
| `get-worksheet-xml` 500s on a dashboard-bound sheet | Retry that sheet once individually. If it still fails, render `on_sheets`/`on_dashboards` for that calc as `unresolved: xml-read-failed` per HC#7; do not fail the whole run. |
| Workbook has 100+ calcs | Ask user to scope; default to all. |
| Workbook has 0 calcs | Exit with No calculated fields found; nothing to document. |
| User asks to fix or apply captions | Refuse per HC#1. Route to Desktop-manual instructions. |
| User asks to explain a specific calc | Refuse per HC#10. Route to `calc-explainer` with handoff payload. |
| User asks to audit calc hygiene | Refuse per HC#10. Route to `calc-linter`. |
| User asks to document multiple workbooks | Refuse per HC#2. |
| User asks to skip V-gate | Refuse per HC#8. |
| User asks to save file without path confirmation | Refuse per HC#12. |
| User asks to omit the reference graph | Refuse per HC#4. Ref graph is a locked dimension. |

## Examples

**Example 1: Compact workbook, mixed calc types.**

User: document my calcs

Skill runs Phases 0-4 silently, delivers Tier A:

```
**Calc Documentation: Sales Overview**
Datasources: 2 · Total calcs: 18 · Graph shape: DAG

Per-datasource TL;DR:
- Orders: 12 calcs, 4 row-level, 6 aggregate, 2 LOD, 5 with author captions
- Returns: 6 calcs, 3 row-level, 3 aggregate, 0 LOD, 2 with author captions

Top 3 most-referenced calcs (used-by count):
1. Profit Ratio: used by 4 other calcs, on 7 sheets
2. Regional Sales YoY: used by 3, on 5 sheets
3. Discount Impact: used by 2, on 3 sheets

Save the full dictionary to Downloads? (.md default, .txt option, or skip)
```

**Example 2: Cyclic dependency detected.**

Skill detects Calc A references Calc B, Calc B references Calc C, Calc C references Calc A. Tier A adds banner:

```
**Cycle detected (CD-CYCLE-01):** Profit Ratio → Discount Impact → Profit Ratio. Chain is not renderable as a valid dependency graph; see full report for details.
```

Marks all three calcs `in_cycle: true` in Tier B.

**Example 3: Refuse to explain.**

User: explain what Profit Ratio does in plain English

Skill: Natural-language explanation of a specific calc is `calc-explainer`s scope. Ive emitted the `calc_documentation/1` handoff with the Profit Ratio entry (formula, refs, usage, aggregation context). Want me to route the request to calc-explainer with the doc payload?

## Relationship to Other Skills

- **Peer to calc-inventory.** Inventory discovers what calcs exist; this skill documents what each one is.
- **Peer to calc-linter.** Linter audits naming and commenting hygiene; this skill emits doc content on top of what exists.
- **Upstream of calc-explainer.** Explainer consumes the reference graph to place a specific calc in context.
- **Upstream of publish-readiness.** Publish-readiness uses author-caption presence as a documentation-completeness signal.

## MCP Skill Mapping

Desktop-native. No MCP dependency. Uses standard Desktop tools (`get-workbook-inventory`, `list-workbook-datasources`, `list-available-fields`, `resolve-field`, `get-worksheet-xml`, `get-dashboard-xml`).

# Calc Explainer — when to use

Source: https://tableau.github.io/tableau-ai-utilities/tableau-studio-skills/tableau-agent/calc-family/calc-explainer

## What it does

Given the name of a calculated field in an open Tableau workbook, produces a compact four-dimension explanation: what the calc computes, why it is structured that way, how it fits with the workbook's other calcs, and what to expect at runtime (row-level vs aggregate behavior, LOD grain, table-calc gotchas). Every sentence cites either the formula, a specific pattern, or a named reference. Read-only. Nothing gets written back to the workbook.

## When to use it

- "I inherited this workbook and I need to understand a specific calc before I touch it"
- "I want to know why this Profit Ratio uses SUM(Profit) / SUM(Sales) instead of AVG(Profit / Sales)"
- "I need to explain a LOD or table calc to a stakeholder in plain English"
- "I want to see which other calcs depend on this one before I edit it"
- "I want the runtime story (row vs aggregate, LOD grain) without opening the calc editor"

## When NOT to use it

- Not for documenting every calc in the workbook (use `calc-documenter` for bulk)
- Not for diagnosing why a calc returns NULL (use `calc-debugger`)
- Not for calc naming, comments, or hygiene audit (use `calc-linter`)
- Not for rewriting a slow calc (use `calc-optimizer`)
- Not for authoring a new calc (use `calc-writer`)
- Not for applying edits (this skill is read-only)

## How to trigger it

- "explain this calc"
- "what does Profit Ratio do"
- "explain Profit Ratio in plain English"
- "walk me through this calculated field"
- "why is this calc structured this way"

# Calc Explainer — SKILL.md

Source: https://tableau.github.io/tableau-ai-utilities/tableau-studio-skills/tableau-agent/calc-family/calc-explainer/SKILL

# Calc Explainer

## When to use (full trigger detail)

Explain a specific Tableau calculated field in plain language. Given a calc name from an open workbook, produces a four-dimension explanation. what it computes (plain language), why it is structured that way (technical rationale), how it fits in the calc family (reference-graph position from calc-documenter handoff if available, or re-derived locally), and what to expect at runtime (row-level vs aggregate behavior, LOD grain, table-calc addressing gotchas). Read-only. Trigger with explain this calc, what does {calc name} do, explain {calc name} in plain English, calc-explainer, walk me through this calculated field, why is this calc structured this way. Do NOT trigger on. bulk documentation of every calc (defer to calc-documenter), calc syntax debugging or NULL diagnosis (defer to calc-debugger), calc naming or hygiene audit (defer to calc-linter), calc optimization or performance rewrites (defer to calc-optimizer), writing or authoring new calcs (defer to calc-writer), applying changes to calc formulas (this skill is read-only), format-string drift on caption fonts (defer to format-drift-scanner).

## Purpose

Explain a single Tableau calculated field in plain language to the workbook author. Four locked dimensions per explanation: what the calc computes (author-facing prose), why it is structured that way (technical rationale citing patterns from `skill-expertise/explanation_patterns.md`), how it fits in the calc family (reference-graph position with parents and children named), and what to expect at runtime (row-level vs aggregate behavior, LOD grain implications, table-calc addressing notes). Read-only. Every explanation cites the formula substring or reference-graph entry that grounds it; no fabrication.

Positioned downstream of calc-documenter in the calc-family pipeline. If `calc_documentation/1` handoff is available in session context, calc-explainer consumes it. Otherwise, calc-explainer re-derives the same signals locally per HC#12.

## Trigger Conditions

- explain this calc
- what does {calc name} do
- explain {calc name} in plain English
- calc-explainer
- walk me through this calculated field
- why is this calc structured this way
- how does {calc name} work
- whats this formula doing

## Do NOT Trigger On

- Bulk documentation of every calc in the workbook (defer to `calc-documenter`).
- Calc syntax debugging or NULL diagnosis (defer to `calc-debugger`).
- Calc naming or hygiene audit (defer to `calc-linter`).
- Calc optimization or performance rewrites (defer to `calc-optimizer`).
- Writing or authoring new calcs (defer to `calc-writer`).
- Applying changes to calc formulas (all fixes are Desktop-manual per HC#1).
- Format-string drift on caption fonts (defer to `format-drift-scanner`).
- Data-quality issues (defer to `data-quality-review`).
- Performance analysis (defer to `calc-optimizer`).

## Scope Boundaries

- **IN.** One calc per run. Name-based lookup from an open workbook via `list-available-fields` + `resolve-field`. Four-dimension explanation. Opportunistic consumption of `calc_documentation/1` handoff when available in session context. Cross-datasource references named but not fully resolved. Read-only. Handoff schema `calc_explanation/1`.
- **OUT.** Any workbook mutation. Bulk-workbook explanation (route to calc-documenter). Calc rewriting or optimization. Explaining a calc that doesnt exist in an open workbook (user must open the workbook or provide the name of a calc that resolves).

**Multi-datasource workbooks.** If the calc name is ambiguous across datasources (same name in two datasources), skill asks one clarifying question (Explain Profit Ratio from Orders or from Returns?) before proceeding.

**Handoff consumption pattern.** If `calc_documentation/1` handoff is in session context AND references the target calc, calc-explainer uses the handoffs reference-graph and aggregation classification. Otherwise, skill re-derives the same signals locally via `list-available-fields`, `resolve-field`, and formula pattern-matching. Report includes `handoff_consumed: true|false` for transparency.

## The 4-Dimension Explanation Model

Every explanation includes these four dimensions in this order:

| # | Dimension | What it answers | Grounded in |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **What it computes** | Plain-language description of the output | Formula verbatim, cited substring per operation |
| 2 | **Why it is structured this way** | Technical rationale for the specific pattern used | Pattern from `explanation_patterns.md` (e.g., SUM-of-ratios pattern for correct aggregation) |
| 3 | **How it fits in the calc family** | Parents (uses), children (used by), and context | Reference graph from handoff or re-derived locally |
| 4 | **What to expect at runtime** | Row-level vs aggregate behavior, LOD grain, table-calc gotchas | Aggregation classification from `calc-documenter`s patterns |

**Explanation length.** Target 3-5 sentences per dimension. Total explanation under 25 lines. No preamble, no meta-commentary, no marketing.

## Workflow Phases

- **Phase 0 Scope.** Confirm workbook is open via `get-workbook-inventory`. Ask user for the calc name if not stated. Resolve via `resolve-field`. If ambiguous across datasources, ask one clarifying question.
- **Phase 1 Handoff Check.** Look for `calc_documentation/1` handoff in session context. If present AND references the target calc, use it for Dimension 3 (reference-graph) and Dimension 4 (aggregation classification). Set `handoff_consumed: true`. Otherwise proceed to Phase 2.
- **Phase 2 Local Extract (if no handoff).** Read formula from `list-available-fields`. Parse formula for field references. Resolve each via `resolve-field`. Classify aggregation via `explanation_patterns.md` precedence rules (same six types as calc-documenter). Build local reference graph by scanning other calcs in the same datasource for references to this calc (used-by list).
- **Phase 3 Compose Explanation.** For each of the four dimensions, generate 3-5 sentences grounded in the extracted signals. Cite formula substrings, referenced calcs, and pattern names.
- **Phase 4 Validate.** Run the 4-check V-gate: dimension coverage, formula citation, handoff-or-local-source labeled, no fabricated references.
- **Phase 5 Deliver.** Compact single-tier chat output. Optional handoff to calc-debugger if user asks about NULL behavior, or to calc-optimizer if user asks about performance.

## Hard Constraints

**HC#1 Read-only always.** Never invoke `author-calc`, `bind-template`, `build-and-apply-worksheet`, or any mutating tool. Explanation is emitted; nothing is written back to the workbook.

**HC#2 One calc per run.** Multi-calc explanations refused; route to `calc-documenter` for bulk. User invokes calc-explainer separately per calc.

**HC#3 Bulk-action refusal.** Explain every calc in my workbook refused; skill is one-calc-per-run. Route to calc-documenter.

**HC#4 Locked four-dimension model.** Every explanation includes all four dimensions in order. No dimension omitted. No fabricated dimension added. If a dimension cannot be populated (e.g., calc has zero references so Dimension 3 has empty parents/children), render the empty state explicitly (No parents; no children) rather than skipping the dimension.

**HC#5 Ground every claim.** Every sentence in the explanation cites either a formula substring, a referenced calc name, or a pattern name from `explanation_patterns.md`. No unsupported generalizations. No this calc probably... language.

**HC#6 Never auto-invoke another skill.** Adjacent-skill routing (calc-debugger for NULLs, calc-optimizer for performance) is an opt-in handoff.

**HC#7 Sentinel discipline.** Use `null` and empty-state prose (No parents; no children) for absent references. Never blank a dimension.

**HC#8 Refuse to fabricate.** V-gate refuses explanations that cite formula substrings not present in the actual formula, or reference calcs not present in the workbook.

**HC#9 Partial-info handling.** If the calcs formula references a field that `resolve-field` cannot locate (deleted, renamed), render as `unresolved: <raw>` and note the resolution failure in Dimension 3 rather than fabricating.

**HC#10 Adjacent-skill routing.** NULL diagnosis → `calc-debugger`. Performance concerns → `calc-optimizer`. Hygiene audit → `calc-linter`. Bulk explanation → `calc-documenter`. Rewriting → `calc-writer`.

**HC#11 Author caption preserved.** If the calc has an existing author caption, quote it verbatim in Dimension 1 as the authors stated intent. Skills explanation supplements the caption; never rewrites, paraphrases, or contradicts it silently. If the skills technical read conflicts with the author caption, note the conflict transparently.

**HC#12 Handoff-or-local-source labeled.** Every explanation includes `signal_source: handoff | local_extract` in the handoff payload. User can tell which path fired without re-reading the reference-graph section.

**HC#13 Guide the user actively.** If the calc name is ambiguous, ask one clarifying question. If the calc doesnt exist, list the closest matches (top 3 by name similarity) and offer to proceed with one.

**HC#14 Grounded prose ordering locked.** Within each dimension, sentences render in this order: (1) claim, (2) formula-substring or reference-graph citation, (3) implication for the reader. Never rearrange. This is the same anchor-first discipline pattern as viz-critique-pro-studio and calc-documenter.

**HC#15 Handoff staleness detection required.** When consuming a `calc_documentation/1` handoff, the target calcs current formula MUST match the handoffs stored formula (byte-exact after whitespace normalization). Mismatch forces `local_extract` fallback per V5 and is logged in `run_metadata.notes`. Never render a handoff-sourced explanation against a stale formula. Author changes to a calc between the handoff run and the explainer run are the primary reason for this rule.

## Single-Tier Delivery

**Chat output only.** No opt-in file save. Explanation lives in chat.

Template:

```
**Calc Explanation: {calc_name}** ({datasource_name})
Signal source: {handoff | local extract}
{Author caption if present, quoted verbatim, one line}

**What it computes.**
{3-5 sentences. Cite formula substrings.}

**Why it is structured this way.**
{3-5 sentences. Cite pattern name from explanation_patterns.md.}

**How it fits in the calc family.**
Parents (uses): {list or none}
Children (used by): {list or none}
{2-3 sentences of context.}

**What to expect at runtime.**
Type: {row-level | aggregate | LOD-fixed | LOD-include | LOD-exclude | table-calc}
{3-5 sentences. Cite aggregation implications, LOD grain, or table-calc addressing.}

Next: {one-line routing suggestion, or no downstream skill recommended.}
```

**Never rendered.** Improvement recommendations (calc-explainer explains, does not recommend fixes; thats calc-optimizers job). Fabricated context. Marketing prose.

**Ancillary file save.** If user asks to save the explanation, offer `.md` or `.txt` in Downloads via the standard opt-in path-confirmation flow. Not the default path.

## Validation Gate (5-Check Read-Only)

**V1 Dimension Coverage.** All four dimensions rendered in order with 3-5 sentences each (or explicit empty-state prose per HC#4/7).

**V2 Formula Citation.** Every claim in Dimension 1 (What it computes) cites a formula substring or aggregation function name. No unsupported prose.

**V3 Reference Grounding.** Every parent/child name in Dimension 3 exists in the workbook (verified via handoff or `resolve-field`). No fabricated references.

**V4 Handoff-or-Local Labeled.** `signal_source` field populated. If handoff was used, target calc must actually appear in the handoffs `datasources[].calcs[]` list.

**V5 Formula-Hash Cross-Check (handoff mode only).** When `signal_source: handoff`, hash the target calcs current formula from `list-available-fields` and compare against the handoffs stored formula for the same calc. If the hashes mismatch, the handoff is stale (calc changed since the handoff was generated). Force fallback to `signal_source: local_extract`, log the drift in `run_metadata.notes` (handoff formula-hash mismatch; fell back to local extract), and re-derive Dimensions 3 and 4 locally. Never render a handoff-sourced explanation against a stale formula.

V-gate failure on V1-V4 blocks delivery per HC#8. V5 does not block delivery; it forces the local_extract fallback and continues.

## Tool Sequence

- **Phase 0.** `get-workbook-inventory` (never twice per run). `list-available-fields` for calc lookup. `resolve-field` on the target calc name.
- **Phase 1.** In-memory handoff check. No tool calls.
- **Phase 2 (if no handoff).** `list-available-fields` on the target datasource for the calcs formula. `resolve-field` per formula reference (batched, 20 per parallel call). For used-by construction: iterate through other calcs in the same datasource and pattern-match for references to the target calc.
- **Phase 3-4.** In-memory composition and validation. No tool calls.
- **Phase 5.** Chat delivery. No tool calls unless the user asks to save the explanation.

**Batching rules.** `resolve-field` batches capped at 20 per parallel call (matches calc-documenter HC#5). Never call `get-workbook-inventory` or `list-available-fields` twice per run.

**Early-exit condition.** If the calc name doesnt resolve after user disambiguation, exit gracefully with Calc {name} not found in the open workbook. Closest matches: {top 3}. Which one?

## Handoff Contract

Emits `calc_explanation/1` per `skill-expertise/handoff_schema.md`. Consumed by:

- **calc-debugger.** Consumes when user routes to NULL diagnosis on the same calc.
- **calc-optimizer.** Consumes when user routes to performance analysis on the same calc.
- **workbook-auditor.** Consumes when tracking explanation deltas across runs (calc changed, explanation shifted).

## Known Limitations

- **No cross-datasource full resolution.** If the calc references a field in another datasource that isnt loaded, Dimension 3 lists the reference as `cross_datasource: {ds_name}.{field_name}` without traversing it.
- **Table-calc addressing.** Skill notes that table calcs have partition/addressing configured on the worksheet, not in the calc XML. Dimension 4 describes the pattern (WINDOW_SUM, RUNNING_SUM, etc.) but does not specify the addressing per worksheet.
- **Author caption conflicts.** If the author caption conflicts with the skills technical read (e.g., caption says returns average but formula is SUM), HC#11 requires transparent flagging. Skill does not decide who is right.
- **`list-available-fields` reliability gap**. If it returns partial results, skill exits with an explicit failure rather than fabricating an explanation.
- **Set / parameter references.** Explained as field references without enumerating set membership or parameter value list.

## Error Handling

| Failure | Response |
|---|---|
| Workbook not open | Ask: Please open the workbook containing the calc youd like explained. |
| Calc name not stated | Ask: Which calc would you like explained? Provide the name from your workbook. |
| Calc name doesnt resolve | List top 3 closest name matches, offer to proceed with one, or exit if user declines. |
| Calc name ambiguous across datasources | Ask one clarifying question with datasource names. |
| `get-workbook-inventory` fails | Retry once. If still failing, exit gracefully. |
| `list-available-fields` returns partial | Exit with explicit failure per Known Limitations; do not fabricate. |
| `resolve-field` returns no match for a formula reference | Render as `unresolved: <raw>` in Dimension 3 per HC#9. |
| Handoff exists but doesnt reference the target calc | Fall back to local extract per HC#12. Note in `signal_source: local_extract`. |
| User asks to explain multiple calcs | Refuse per HC#2. Route to calc-documenter for bulk. |
| User asks to fix or rewrite the calc | Refuse per HC#1 and HC#10. Route to calc-writer or calc-optimizer. |
| User asks to skip a dimension | Refuse per HC#4. Four-dimension model is locked. |
| User asks for performance analysis of the calc | Refuse per HC#10. Route to calc-optimizer with the explanation payload. |
| User asks about NULL behavior of the calc | Offer to route to calc-debugger; do not diagnose here. |

## Examples

**Example 1: Aggregate calc with handoff.**

User (workbook open with calc_documentation/1 in session): explain Profit Ratio

Skill runs Phase 0 (resolve), Phase 1 (handoff hit), skips Phase 2, composes:

```
**Calc Explanation: Profit Ratio** (Orders)
Signal source: handoff
Author caption: Overall profit margin, aggregate not row-level.

**What it computes.**
Profit Ratio returns the ratio of total profit to total sales, aggregated to whatever grain the worksheet is displaying. Formula: `SUM([Profit]) / SUM([Sales])`. The numerator sums profit across the current row context; the denominator sums sales across the same context.

**Why it is structured this way.**
SUM-of-ratios avoids the average-of-averages pitfall (Pattern: agg-first-then-divide). If the calc were `AVG([Profit] / [Sales])`, each rows ratio would be averaged, which is arithmetically wrong for a portfolio-level margin. The SUM-then-divide pattern respects the underlying dollars.

**How it fits in the calc family.**
Parents (uses): [Profit], [Sales]
Children (used by): Regional Profit YoY, Discount Impact Score, Top 10 Profit Filter
Profit Ratio is a mid-level utility calc; two of its three children are dashboard-facing.

**What to expect at runtime.**
Type: aggregate
Aggregate calcs cannot be placed on Detail; must go on a shelf with a partition context (e.g., Region on Rows). If you try to filter by Profit Ratio directly at the row level, Tableau will refuse and offer to aggregate first. LOD grain matters: this calc respects the shelf-defined grain.

Next: If you need to diagnose why Profit Ratio returns NULL for a specific segment, route to calc-debugger.
```

**Example 2: Row-level calc, no handoff.**

User (workbook open, no prior calc-documenter run): explain Discount Impact

Skill runs Phase 0 + Phase 2 (local extract) + Phases 3-4. Renders same 4-dimension shape with `signal_source: local_extract`.

**Example 3: Ambiguous calc name.**

User: explain Growth Rate

Skill: Growth Rate appears in two datasources: Orders and Returns. Which one?

User: Orders

Skill proceeds normally with `datasource: Orders`.

**Example 4: Calc doesnt exist.**

User: explain Return Rate

Skill: No calc named Return Rate in the open workbook. Closest matches: Return Ratio (Returns), Rate of Return (Orders), Return Percentage (Orders). Which one, or should I exit?

## Relationship to Other Skills

- **Downstream of calc-documenter.** Consumes `calc_documentation/1` handoff when available for reference-graph and aggregation context.
- **Peer to calc-debugger.** Explainer describes what the calc does; debugger diagnoses why it isnt doing it. NULL diagnosis routes to debugger.
- **Peer to calc-optimizer.** Explainer describes the pattern; optimizer proposes a faster equivalent. Performance concerns route to optimizer.
- **Upstream of workbook-auditor.** Auditor consumes explanation deltas across runs for change tracking.

## MCP Skill Mapping

Desktop-native. No MCP dependency. Uses standard Desktop tools (`get-workbook-inventory`, `list-available-fields`, `resolve-field`).

## Graceful Degradation

These rules apply whenever something this skill needs is missing or fails. More specific rules elsewhere in this file take precedence.

- **Nothing to work on.** If no workbook is open, there is no data source, or the named calc, sheet, dashboard, or data source isn't found, stop before any other step. Say what you found (list the real names, if any) and ask the user to open the workbook or pick one. Never work on a guessed or closest-match target.
- **Tool call fails, times out, or returns empty.** Retry once, then stop retrying. Mark everything that depended on that call as not checked, continue with what you still can, and say which step failed. If the failed call was a write, stop and report the workbook's current state instead of continuing.
- **Partial results.** If any check, sheet, field, or data source wasn't evaluated, the summary says so (Partial: N of M checked; not checked: [list]). Never give a clean, ready, or PASS verdict on a partial run.
- **Reference file won't open.** Use the rules summarized in this file, say [file] unavailable; using the built-in summary, and never make up thresholds, rule IDs, or Desktop menu steps from memory.
- **Peer skill not installed.** If this skill would hand off to another skill that isn't available, say so and give the manual Desktop step instead. A handoff is never the only next step.
- **Platform gap.** If no tool can do something, say so plainly and give the manual Desktop path.
- **Failure messages.** Tell the user in plain language what was done, what wasn't, and the next step. No raw errors, stack traces, or JSON.
- **No fabrication.** Never invent fields, values, findings, or results to fill a gap left by a failed read.

# Data Model Documenter — when to use

Source: https://tableau.github.io/tableau-ai-utilities/tableau-studio-skills/tableau-agent/build-and-design/data-model-documenter

## What it does

The logical model lives inside the .twb and is hard to share. Documenter reads workbook state, extracts the model, and produces a single shareable markdown output. Deterministic; two runs on the same source produce the same file (modulo row-count sample variance on live sources).

## When to use it

- "Document this data model."
- "Export the tables and relationships."
- "Share this data source structure."
- "Make a data model doc for handoff."

## When NOT to use it

- Field-meaning documentation (use `data-scribe`).
- Change tracking over time (use `workbook-auditor`).
- Recommending model changes (use `join-and-relationship-advisor`).
- Connection setup (use `data-source-connector`).
- Data-content audit (use `data-quality-review`).
