# Chart Swap Advisor — SKILL.md

Source: https://tableau.github.io/tableau-ai-utilities/tableau-studio-skills/tableau-agent/content-quality/chart-swap-advisor/SKILL

# Chart Swap Advisor

## When to use (full trigger detail)

Evaluate one Tableau worksheet against its question type and recommend a chart-type swap when the current chart is a poor fit. Classifies the question type against the shared 9-type taxonomy (Temporal, Categorical, Composition, Distribution, Correlation, Ranking, Geographic, Status/KPI, Sequential), reads the actual mark type from XML, compares against the locked recommendation catalog, and produces a swap recommendation with rationale plus a handoff to Worksheet Builder for the rebuild. Read-only advisory. Trigger with should this be a different chart, chart swap, is this the right chart type, recommend a better chart, chart-swap-advisor. Do NOT trigger on. building a new chart from scratch (defer to worksheet-builder), explaining what a chart is currently doing (defer to logic-explainer), dashboard-level chart-mix advisory across multiple sheets (defer to viz-planner), data-quality issues (defer to data-quality-review).

## Purpose

Evaluate one Tableau worksheets chart-type fit against its question type. Read-only advisory. Recommends a swap when the current chart mismatches the question, or a Keep verdict when the fit is right. Every recommendation is a Worksheet Builder rebuild instruction the user opts into.

Sits parallel to Worksheet Builder in the pipeline. Worksheet Builder authors new charts from natural language. Chart Swap Advisor evaluates existing charts and hands off to Worksheet Builder for the rebuild.

## Trigger Conditions

- should this be a different chart
- chart swap
- is this the right chart type
- recommend a better chart
- chart-swap-advisor
- evaluate this chart
- wrong chart for this question
- audit this charts type

## Do NOT Trigger On

- Building a new chart from scratch (defer to `worksheet-builder`).
- Explaining what a chart is currently doing without recommending a swap (defer to `logic-explainer`).
- Dashboard-level chart-mix advisory across multiple sheets (defer to `viz-planner`).
- Data-quality issues in the underlying data (defer to `data-quality-review`).
- Dashboard assembly hygiene (defer to `dashboard-preflight`).
- Format-string drift on the current chart (defer to `format-drift-scanner`).
- Calc-behind-the-chart authoring or debugging (defer to calc-orchestrator).
- Change-over-time on the chart (defer to `workbook-auditor`).

## Scope Boundaries

- **IN.** One worksheet per run. Question-type classification against the 9-type taxonomy. Mark-type read from `get-worksheet-xml`. Anti-pattern detection (3D, pie >5 slices, dual-axis when single-axis suffices). Audience-override honoring when audience is stated. Swap recommendation with rationale. Handoff to `worksheet-builder` for the rebuild. Read-only output. Handoff schema `chart_swap_recommendation/1`.
- **OUT.** Any workbook mutation. Rebuilding the chart directly. Evaluating multiple worksheets in one run. Dashboard-level chart-mix advisory. Data-quality issues. Format-string drift.

**Cross-datasource worksheets.** Chart type is a worksheet-level property, so DS count doesnt change the audit. If the worksheet blends multiple DS, note that in the handoff but dont downgrade the recommendation.

**Scale bands.**

- **Simple worksheet (single measure + single dimension).** Full audit. No optimizations needed.
- **Typical worksheet (2-4 measures, 1-3 dimensions).** Full audit.
- **Complex worksheet (5+ measures, 4+ dimensions, dual-axis, calc-heavy).** Full audit. Flag complexity as a signal but do not downgrade the recommendation.
- **Multiple mark types on one worksheet (dual-axis, MARKS card multi-mark).** Evaluate each mark separately and produce a per-mark recommendation. Info-severity if only one aligns.
- **Sparse-signal worksheet (1-2 fields total, or a single row of data).** Classification confidence caps at Low regardless of field pattern — too few signals to trust a Medium/High tag. Report Low confidence with the specific missing signals named, per HC#4.

## Workflow Phases

- **Phase 0 Scope.** Identify the target worksheet. If the workbook contains multiple worksheets and the user did not name one, ask which one. Reuse `get-workbook-inventory` output if a prior skill already called it. **Override points:** the user may state upfront to force a full re-scan (skip diff-mode reuse) or to scope to a stated audience/question type immediately (skip classification per HC#5) — honor these without asking a follow-up. **Prior-report reuse:** if a `chart_swap_recommendation/1` handoff for this worksheet exists in session context (or on disk next to the workbook), offer to diff against it rather than re-scan. Diff-mode trigger map:
  - Mark type changed since the prior report (rebuild happened) → full re-scan.
  - Field list on the worksheet changed (measures/dimensions added or removed) → full re-scan.
  - Audience specification changed (user restates target audience) → full re-scan.
  - Session conversation references a rebuild (I just switched Sales Trend to a line chart) → re-scan that worksheet.
  - If none of the above changed, reuse the prior recommendation verbatim and note diff-mode in the report.
- **Phase 1 Inventory.** Read the worksheets mark type, shelf-placement inventory (Rows, Columns, Marks, Filters, Detail), current view fit, and field references via `get-worksheet-xml` and `list-available-fields`. For multiple mark types (dual-axis, multi-mark), inventory each separately.
- **Phase 2 Classify.** Assign a question type from the locked 9-type taxonomy per the classification rules in `skill-expertise/question_type_taxonomy.md`. Use a three-tier confidence tag (High/Medium/Low) matching Logic Explainers convention.
- **Phase 3 Evaluate.** Compare current mark type against the recommended default for the classified question type per `skill-expertise/chart_recommendation_catalog.md`. Run the anti-pattern gate against `skill-expertise/anti_patterns.md` (3D auto-block, pie >5 slices auto-block, dual-axis when single-axis suffices Warning, executive-audience-with-analytical-chart Warning).
- **Phase 4 Recommend.** Assemble a swap recommendation with: verdict (Keep / Swap Recommended / Anti-Pattern Block), rationale (question type + confidence tag + why the current chart mismatches or matches), recommended chart type, and Worksheet Builder handoff payload. Report shape follows `skill-expertise/report_template.md`.
- **Phase 5 Deliver.** Compact chat summary first (verdict + current vs. recommended + confidence). Offer to write the full report to Downloads (`.md` or `.txt`).

## The 9-Type Question Taxonomy (Shared with Worksheet Builder)

Full detail lives in `skill-expertise/question_type_taxonomy.md` and duplicates Worksheet Builders `decision_framework.md` intentionally. Summary:

| Type | Signal Words / Field Combinations | Default Chart |
|---|---|---|
| Temporal | trend, over time, by month/year; continuous date dimension on Columns | Line |
| Categorical | compare, across, by [dimension]; discrete dimension on Rows/Columns, measure on the other | Horizontal bar (sorted) |
| Composition | breakdown, share, proportion; measure with dimension breaking it out; sum-to-100% intent | Stacked bar or treemap |
| Distribution | distribution, spread, histogram; single measure with binning intent | Histogram |
| Correlation | relationship, vs., correlation; two measures on Rows and Columns | Scatter |
| Ranking | top, bottom, rank, best/worst; measure sorted by discrete dimension, Top N filter | Sorted horizontal bar + Top N |
| Geographic | by state/city/country, map, where; geographic role on a dimension | Filled map (choropleth) |
| Status/KPI | KPI, target, actual vs., on track; single measure, minimal dimensions | KPI tile or bullet chart |
| Sequential | funnel, pipeline, stages, flow; ordered discrete dimension with a natural sequence | Funnel (sorted bar with stages) |

## Anti-Pattern Gate (Locked)

Full detail in `skill-expertise/anti_patterns.md`. Summary:

- **3D chart (any type).** Auto-block. Every question type has a superior 2D alternative.
- **Pie chart with >5 slices.** Auto-block. Recommend stacked bar or treemap.
- **Dual-axis when single-axis suffices.** Warning. Recommend single-axis unless dual-axis serves a specific decision (comparing two measures on different scales for the same dimension).
- **Executive audience with analytical chart.** Warning when audience is stated as Executive AND current chart is scatter, distribution, or correlation. Suggest KPI or ranked bar.
- **Word cloud, packed bubbles, radar, gauge (any).** Auto-block for stakeholder-facing dashboards. Recommend a domain-appropriate alternative.
- **Text table when a chart would answer faster.** Warning if question type is Temporal, Ranking, or Correlation and current mark is Text.

## Hard Constraints

**HC#1 Read-only always.** Never invoke `bind-template`, `build-and-apply-worksheet`, `author-calc`, `add-field`, `remove-field`, or any mutating tool. Every recommendation is a Worksheet Builder handoff or a manual Desktop instruction the user applies.

**HC#2 One worksheet per run.** Multi-worksheet advisory is refused. Users invoke separately per worksheet, or route to `viz-planner` for dashboard-level chart-mix.

**HC#3 Bulk-action refusal.** If the user asks to recommend swaps for every worksheet or swap all my charts, refuse and route: one worksheet per run. For workbooks with many worksheets, this means repeated single-run invocations is the expected pattern, not a limitation to work around.

**HC#4 No fabricated question type.** Every question-type classification cites specific signals (field types, dimension positions, signal words in the worksheet name or caption) with a three-tier confidence tag. Low-confidence classifications explicitly say closest match is X but the signal is weak; consider re-running with a stated question or audience.

**HC#5 User-named-question-type wins.** If the user says this is a Temporal question or audit this as a Ranking chart, honor the stated question type and skip the classification phase. Still run the anti-pattern gate and the recommendation.

**HC#6 Never simulate the rebuild.** Chart Swap Advisor never rebuilds the chart. The handoff to `worksheet-builder` is a payload the user must accept before any rebuild happens. Do not chain into worksheet-builder automatically.

**HC#7 Sentinel discipline.** Use `null`, `[]`, `unscanned` for missing data. Never blank fields in the handoff schema.

**HC#8 Refuse to fabricate.** If the V-gate cannot pass after one retry, refuse delivery and diagnose. Never fake a V-gate pass. Never invent a question-type signal to reach a Medium or High confidence tag.

**HC#9 Partial-info handling.** If the users ask includes partial context (audit this chart but assume Executive audience), honor the stated audience and note that in the handoff. If the audience conflicts with observable field usage (Executive with 8 measures on the sheet), note the conflict and recommend a swap that resolves both.

**HC#10 Adjacent-skill routing.** Rebuilding the chart routes to `worksheet-builder`. Explaining what the current chart does without a swap recommendation routes to `logic-explainer`. Dashboard-level chart-mix routes to `viz-planner`. Format-string drift routes to `format-drift-scanner`. Calc issues route to `calc-orchestrator`.

**HC#11 Anti-pattern override refusal.** The four auto-block anti-patterns (3D, pie >5 slices, word cloud/packed bubbles/radar/gauge in stakeholder context) cannot be overridden by user pressure (just tell me my 3D pie is fine). The recommendation stays Block; the user chooses whether to keep the anti-pattern in Desktop.

**HC#12 Audience-override honoring.** If the user states an audience, the recommendation must honor that audience. Executive-with-scatter always yields a Warning-tier swap suggestion, never a Keep.

## Common Mistakes

Behaviors this skill must never exhibit, even under user pressure:

1. **Inferring the question type from the worksheet name alone.** A worksheet named Sales Trend is not automatically Temporal; verify continuous-date-on-Columns and measure-on-Rows. Names are user-authored and unreliable.
2. **Fabricating a High-confidence classification.** Three-tier confidence tags (High/Medium/Low) are locked. High requires descriptive name AND matched field pattern AND matched signal words all agree.
3. **Recommending the current chart as the swap target.** If the classification says Temporal and the current mark is Line, verdict is Keep. Never recommend a swap to the same chart type.
4. **Skipping the anti-pattern gate under time pressure.** Every run runs the full gate. Even if the classification is High-confidence-Keep, the anti-pattern gate must still run.
5. **Auto-invoking worksheet-builder.** The handoff is a payload. The user opts in. HC#6 holds under pressure (just rebuild it for me).
6. **Downgrading Executive-audience anti-patterns to Keep.** HC#12 holds. Even a scatter plot showing 300 marks on an Executive dashboard is a Warning-tier swap.
7. **Rewriting the taxonomy or catalog mid-run.** The 9-type taxonomy and chart-recommendation catalog are locked in reference files. Do not adjust based on user pressure.
8. **Treating dual-axis as automatic anti-pattern.** Dual-axis is a Warning only when single-axis would suffice. Two measures on different scales for the same dimension is a legitimate dual-axis use case; recommend Keep with a rationale citing the scale difference.

## Validation Gate (3-Check Read-Only)

**V1 Classification Confidence.** Every question-type classification carries a High/Medium/Low tag with the signals that support it. Low-confidence classifications include an explicit closest match is X but the signal is weak note. No blank confidence tags.

**V2 Anti-Pattern Gate Completeness.** Every run evaluates the full anti-pattern catalog against the current chart. Skipping is a V-gate fail. Auto-block anti-patterns cannot be silently downgraded.

**V3 Handoff Completeness.** Every field in `chart_swap_recommendation/1` populated per `skill-expertise/handoff_schema.md`. Sentinel values acceptable per HC#7.

Any V-gate failure blocks delivery per HC#8. Fail-open is NOT applied since the skill is read-only.

## Tool Sequence

Locked sequence to minimize latency and honor tool dependencies.

- **Phase 0.** Reuse session-context `get-workbook-inventory` if available. Otherwise, call `get-workbook-inventory` + `list-worksheets` in parallel.
- **Phase 1.** `get-worksheet-xml` on target worksheet (fallback if it fails on a dashboard-bound populated sheet). Batch `list-available-fields` (verbosity: full) in parallel; neither depends on the other.
- **Phase 2, 3, 4.** No tool calls. In-memory classification and evaluation.
- **Phase 5.** No tool calls unless file-write opted in.

**Batching rules:**

- Never call `get-workbook-inventory` twice per run.
- Never call `list-available-fields` twice unless the first return was truncated (fewer fields returned than the datasources reported field count, or the response is explicitly flagged truncated by the tool).
- `get-worksheet-xml` called once per target worksheet. For multi-mark worksheets, the same XML call covers every mark; do not re-call.
- `resolve-field` only if a fields role (measure vs. dimension) is ambiguous from `list-available-fields`; do not resolve every field.

**Early-exit condition.** If Phase 1 inventory returns a worksheet with zero fields (empty shell), skip Phases 2-4, deliver empty worksheet report, and route to `worksheet-builder` per HC#10.

## Handoff Contract

Emits `chart_swap_recommendation/1` per `skill-expertise/handoff_schema.md`. Consumed by:

- **worksheet-builder.** Rebuild payload with recommended mark type + shelf-placement suggestions + rationale.
- **viz-planner.** Dashboard-level chart-mix advisory can consume multiple recommendations.
- **workbook-auditor.** Chart-swap recommendations enrich change digests when the user rebuilds.

## Known Limitations

- `get-worksheet-xml` reliability on dashboard-bound populated sheets (platform gap). Fallback: use `list-available-fields` formula text plus dashboard-XML hints. Findings flagged UNSCANNED when the fallback still fails.
- Cannot verify visual result of the current chart. Sees mark type + shelf-placement, not rendered output.
- Cannot detect chart-type issues that require pixel-level judgment (label overlap, tick-mark spacing, color-blindness contrast).
- Cannot recommend chart types outside the locked 9-type taxonomy without a catalog revision.
- One worksheet per run. Batching refused per HC#3.

## Error Handling

| Failure | Response |
|---|---|
| `get-workbook-inventory` fails | Report tool failure, ask user to reopen workbook. Do not proceed. |
| `list-worksheets` fails | Retry once. If still failing, refuse delivery and diagnose. |
| `get-worksheet-xml` fails on dashboard-bound sheet | Fallback to `list-available-fields` formula text + dashboard-XML hints discipline. Flag mark-type inference as UNSCANNED if fallback still fails. |
| Multi-worksheet workbook, user did not name target | Ask one clarifying question with worksheet names. |
| User asks recommend swaps for all my worksheets | Refuse per HC#3. Suggest one-at-a-time invocation. |
| Workbook has zero worksheets | Report that there is nothing to evaluate. Do not proceed. |
| User asks to rebuild the chart directly | Refuse per HC#1 and HC#6. Route to worksheet-builder with the handoff payload. |
| User asks to override an auto-block anti-pattern | Refuse per HC#11. Recommendation stays Block; user decides in Desktop. |
| Worksheet has zero fields (empty shell) | Report empty worksheet with no findings. Route to worksheet-builder. |
| Mark type is Automatic and mark-detection heuristics disagree | Flag confidence tag as Low. Explain in the report which mark type Tableau would render based on shelf-placement inference. |
| Datasource disconnects mid-run | Flag classification confidence as UNSCANNED if the DS is needed for signal detection. Do not retry the connection. |
| Field-level permission denial (RLS) blocks a field | Flag the specific field UNSCANNED with `reason: fallback_unavailable`. Never treat as absence. |

## Examples

**Example 1: Right chart, Keep verdict.** User: Should this be a different chart? Target worksheet has continuous date on Columns, SUM(Sales) on Rows, Line mark. Classification: Temporal (High confidence: name Sales Trend + continuous-date-on-Columns + measure-on-Rows). Anti-pattern gate clean. Verdict: **Keep**. Rationale: Line chart is the recommended default for Temporal questions. Current placement matches best practice.

**Example 2: Swap recommended.** User: Is this the right chart? Target has SUM(Sales) on Rows, Category dimension on Columns, sorted descending, Text mark. Classification: Categorical (High confidence). Anti-pattern gate: Text-when-chart-would-answer-faster fires as Warning. Verdict: **Swap Recommended**. Recommendation: horizontal sorted bar. Rationale: Categorical comparison reads faster in a sorted bar than in a text table. Preserves the sort order; swap the mark to Bar and move the measure to Columns for horizontal layout.

**Example 3: Anti-pattern auto-block.** User: Audit my chart. Target has three measures in a 3D pie chart with 8 slices. Classification: Composition (High confidence). Anti-pattern gate: 3D auto-block AND pie-with-8-slices auto-block. Verdict: **Anti-Pattern Block**. Recommendation: stacked bar or treemap. Rationale cites both anti-patterns.

**Example 4: Executive audience override.** User: This is for the executive team. Should the chart change? Target has a scatter plot with 300 marks. Classification: Correlation (High confidence). Anti-pattern gate: Executive-with-analytical-chart Warning fires per HC#12. Verdict: **Swap Recommended (audience-driven)**. Recommendation: KPI tile with correlation coefficient or top-5 outlier ranked bar. Rationale: Scatter plots require analytical time-budget; Executive audience has 5-30 seconds. A KPI or ranked bar delivers the same insight in the available window.

**Example 5: Bulk-action refusal.** User: Recommend swaps for every worksheet in this workbook. Agent refuses per HC#3: One worksheet per run. Which worksheet first? Workbook contains: Sales Trend, Regional Detail, Product Mix, Customer Ranking, Order Details. If you want dashboard-level chart-mix advisory, route to viz-planner.

## Relationship to Other Skills

- **Upstream of worksheet-builder.** Chart Swap Advisors handoff is a rebuild payload; worksheet-builder consumes and rebuilds.
- **Peer to logic-explainer.** Logic Explainer explains what a chart does; Chart Swap Advisor evaluates whether the chart is right for the question.
- **Peer to viz-planner.** Chart Swap Advisor owns single-worksheet swaps; Viz Planner owns dashboard-level chart-mix decisions.
- **Adjacent to dashboard-preflight.** Preflight owns view-fit legality per chart type (P-FIT-07); Chart Swap Advisor owns whether the chart type itself is right.
- **Never overlaps with data-quality-review, data-scribe, or calc-family.**

## MCP Skill Mapping

Desktop-native. No MCP dependency.

## Graceful Degradation

These rules apply whenever something this skill needs is missing or fails. More specific rules elsewhere in this file take precedence.

- **Nothing to work on.** If no workbook is open, there is no data source, or the named calc, sheet, dashboard, or data source isn't found, stop before any other step. Say what you found (list the real names, if any) and ask the user to open the workbook or pick one. Never work on a guessed or closest-match target.
- **Tool call fails, times out, or returns empty.** Retry once, then stop retrying. Mark everything that depended on that call as not checked, continue with what you still can, and say which step failed. If the failed call was a write, stop and report the workbook's current state instead of continuing.
- **Partial results.** If any check, sheet, field, or data source wasn't evaluated, the summary says so (Partial: N of M checked; not checked: [list]). Never give a clean, ready, or PASS verdict on a partial run.
- **Reference file won't open.** Use the rules summarized in this file, say [file] unavailable; using the built-in summary, and never make up thresholds, rule IDs, or Desktop menu steps from memory.
- **Peer skill not installed.** If this skill would hand off to another skill that isn't available, say so and give the manual Desktop step instead. A handoff is never the only next step.
- **Platform gap.** If no tool can do something, say so plainly and give the manual Desktop path.
- **Failure messages.** Tell the user in plain language what was done, what wasn't, and the next step. No raw errors, stack traces, or JSON.
- **No fabrication.** Never invent fields, values, findings, or results to fill a gap left by a failed read.

# Dashboard Caption Audit — when to use

Source: https://tableau.github.io/tableau-ai-utilities/tableau-studio-skills/tableau-agent/content-quality/dashboard-caption-audit

## What it does

Scans every dashboard, worksheet, and text object in an open Tableau workbook for title and caption hygiene against an eight-rule completeness catalog. Catches missing titles, missing captions, empty text objects, default names in English / French / Spanish / German, device-layout inheritance duplicates, and placeholder-title text like `<Sheet Name>` that Tableau leaves in when you disable auto-title. Read-only. Every finding is a manual Desktop-fix instruction; you apply the fix. Two-tier delivery: compact chat summary plus opt-in file save.

## When to use it

- "I have a workbook that ships with 'Sheet 1' worksheet titles and I want to catch them before publish"
- "I want to run a monthly QA sweep across a governance library for caption completeness"
- "I'm auditing device-layout variants (phone / tablet) and want to know which ones inherit stale defaults from desktop"
- "I need a prioritized list of caption gaps for a workbook I'm about to hand off"
- "I want to verify a workbook has no placeholder title text before it goes to a stakeholder"

## When NOT to use it

- Not for spellcheck or typography (use `desktop-spellcheck` for text hygiene)
- Not for tooltip content audit (out of scope)
- Not for caption position or sizing sanity (out of scope)
- Not for format-string drift on caption fonts (use `format-drift-scanner`)
- Not for dashboard assembly hygiene like zone alignment or filter-action wiring (use `dashboard-preflight`)
- Not for calc-family metadata audit (use `calc-linter`)

## How to trigger it

- "caption audit"
- "check my titles and captions"
- "audit dashboard captions"
- "dashboard-caption-audit"
- "find missing titles in this workbook"

# Dashboard Caption Audit — SKILL.md

Source: https://tableau.github.io/tableau-ai-utilities/tableau-studio-skills/tableau-agent/content-quality/dashboard-caption-audit/SKILL

# Dashboard Caption Audit

## When to use (full trigger detail)

Audit a Tableau workbook for missing or default titles and captions across dashboards, worksheets, dashboard text objects, and phone/tablet device-layout variants. Runs a locked completeness catalog (dashboard-title-missing, dashboard-caption-missing, worksheet-title-missing, worksheet-caption-missing, text-object-empty, default-name, device-layout-inheritance-duplicate, placeholder-title-text) per dashboard, groups findings by severity, and produces a Desktop-fix report. Read-only. Title and caption completeness only, no tooltip content, no position sanity, no spellcheck (defers to desktop-spellcheck). Trigger with audit captions, check my titles, are my dashboards labeled, caption audit, missing titles, dashboard-caption-audit. Do NOT trigger on. text-copy correctness or spelling (defer to desktop-spellcheck), tooltip content quality (defer to viz-critique-pro-studio), localization or hard-coded strings (defer to i18n-scanner), format-string drift on numbers/dates/fonts (defer to format-drift-scanner), chart-type-only advisory (defer to chart-swap-advisor), pre-publish assembly hygiene (defer to dashboard-preflight), calc issues (defer to calc-orchestrator).

## Purpose

Scan a Tableau workbook for missing or default titles and captions across every dashboard, every worksheet on those dashboards, and every dashboard text object. Read-only. Every finding cites a locked completeness rule and produces a Desktop-fix instruction, never a mutation.

Positioned parallel to desktop-spellcheck and format-drift-scanner in the pipeline. Spellcheck owns text-copy correctness. Format-drift-scanner owns cross-worksheet format-string consistency. Dashboard-caption-audit owns title and caption completeness (are the labels there at all, and did the author actually set them).

**Scope note.** Covers caption and title completeness only. Tooltip content is a viz-critique-pro-studio concern, and position sanity needs pixel-level rendering, which the agent can't do.

## Trigger Conditions

- audit captions
- check my titles
- are my dashboards labeled
- caption audit
- missing titles
- dashboard-caption-audit
- title completeness
- check labels on my workbook

## Do NOT Trigger On

- Text-copy correctness or spelling (defer to `desktop-spellcheck`).
- Tooltip content quality (defer to `viz-critique-pro-studio`).
- Localization fragility or hard-coded strings (defer to `i18n-scanner`).
- Format-string drift on numbers, dates, or fonts (defer to `format-drift-scanner`).
- Chart-type advisory (defer to `chart-swap-advisor`).
- Pre-publish assembly hygiene (defer to `dashboard-preflight`).
- Calc issues (defer to `calc-orchestrator`).
- Applying caption changes (all fixes are Desktop-manual per HC#1).
- Whole-workbook pre-publish hygiene (defer to `publish-readiness`).
- Change-over-time (defer to `workbook-auditor`).

## Scope Boundaries

- **IN.** One workbook per run. Every dashboard, worksheet on those dashboards, and dashboard text object audited for title + caption completeness. Default-name detection (`Dashboard 1`, `Sheet 1`, and locale variants). Locked severity tiers per completeness catalog. Read-only. Per-dashboard TL;DR banner in chat, full findings in opt-in Downloads file. Handoff schema `caption_audit_report/1`.
- **OUT.** Any workbook mutation. Applying caption or title changes. Tooltip content evaluation. Spellcheck of caption text. Format-drift on caption fonts. Position sanity or overlap detection.

**Text objects on the dashboard canvas.** In scope for completeness (empty text object with no content fires `text-object-empty`). Text object content quality is out of scope (defers to viz-critique-pro-studio for design and desktop-spellcheck for spelling).

**Cross-dashboard workbooks.** Each dashboard audited independently. Default naming on one dashboard does not affect scoring of another. TL;DR renders one line per dashboard.

## The 8-Rule Completeness Catalog

Full detail lives in `skill-expertise/completeness_catalog.md`. Summary:

| Rule ID | Trigger | Severity |
|---|---|---|
| DC-TITLE-01 Dashboard-Title-Missing | Dashboard has no title text OR title is hidden AND caption also missing | Warning |
| DC-CAPTION-02 Dashboard-Caption-Missing | Dashboard has no caption text | Info |
| DC-WS-TITLE-03 Worksheet-Title-Missing | Worksheet on a dashboard has no title text OR title is hidden | Warning |
| DC-WS-CAPTION-04 Worksheet-Caption-Missing | Worksheet on a dashboard has no caption text | Info |
| DC-TEXT-EMPTY-05 Text-Object-Empty | Dashboard text object has no content | Warning |
| DC-DEFAULT-NAME-06 Default-Name | Dashboard or worksheet name matches auto-generated pattern (`Dashboard \d+`, `Sheet \d+`, and locale variants) | Warning |
| DC-DEVICE-07 Device-Layout-Inheritance-Duplicate | Desktop parent has missing title or caption AND phone/tablet variant inherits (no device-specific override) | Warning |
| DC-TITLE-08 Placeholder-Title-Text | Dashboard or worksheet title text is Tableaus unedited literal boilerplate (e.g. `<Sheet Name>`, `<Dashboard Name>`) | Warning |

**Warning severity** for missing titles, empty text objects, default names, and device-layout inheritance defects because these reach the end user on Desktop or on phone/tablet. **Info severity** for missing captions because captions are optional in most published workbooks and their absence is a design choice more often than a defect.

Default names are Warning-tier because they signal the author never set an intentional label; the audience sees `Dashboard 1` and reads it as unfinished work.

Device-layout inheritance duplicates are reported **once on the Desktop parent**, with affected variants (phone, tablet) listed in the same finding record. One Desktop-fix path resolves all inherited variants.

## Workflow Phases

- **Phase 0 Scope.** Confirm workbook is open via `get-workbook-inventory`. If not open, ask user to open it. Enumerate every dashboard via `list-dashboards`; enumerate every worksheet on each dashboard via `get-dashboard-xml`. Ask which dashboard(s) to audit only if the workbook has 10+ dashboards (default: all).
- **Phase 1 Inventory.** For each dashboard: read `get-dashboard-xml` for title/caption XML and text-object elements. For each worksheet on the dashboard: read `get-worksheet-xml` for title/caption XML. Batch by dashboard per HC#5 (10 sheets per parallel `get-worksheet-xml` call, sequence remaining).
- **Phase 2 Detect Completeness.** Apply the 8-rule catalog to every dashboard, worksheet, and text object. Every failing element gets its own finding record (do not collapse multiple worksheet-level failures under one rule into a single finding) — a dashboard with 3 worksheets missing titles reports 3 DC-WS-TITLE-03 findings, one per worksheet, matching the per-element counts shown in the Tier A/B templates. Do not fabricate findings; every rule fire cites specific XML evidence.
- **Phase 3 Assemble Report.** Group findings by dashboard (primary) then by severity (Warning → Info). Every finding includes a Desktop-fix instruction. Report shape follows `skill-expertise/report_template.md`.
- **Phase 4 Deliver Tier A.** Compact chat summary: one-line TL;DR per dashboard, then top 3 recommendations across the workbook, then file-save offer. If the workbook has more than 8 dashboards, render TL;DR lines for the first 8 in enumeration order and collapse the remainder into a single `+ {N} more (see full report)` line; Tier B always renders every dashboard regardless of this collapse. Top-3 selection is locked (HC#14): sort all findings by severity (Warning before Info), then by dashboard enumeration order (as returned by `list-dashboards`), then by rule ID ascending (`DC-TITLE-01` before `DC-DEFAULT-NAME-06`, etc.); take the first 3. Ties never depend on judgment.
- **Phase 5 Deliver Tier B (opt-in).** Full findings written to Downloads as `.md` (default) or `.txt` only after user confirms path.

## Hard Constraints

**HC#1 Read-only always.** Never invoke `bind-template`, `build-and-apply-worksheet`, `author-calc`, or any mutating tool. Every recommendation is Desktop-manual.

**HC#2 One workbook per run.** Multi-workbook audits refused. Users invoke separately.

**HC#3 Bulk-action refusal.** Fix all missing captions refused; skill is read-only per HC#1.

**HC#4 Locked catalog.** Every finding cites one of the 8 rule IDs. No fabricated rules. No severity reassignment mid-run.

**HC#5 Batching cap.** `get-worksheet-xml` batches capped at 10 sheets per parallel call regardless of workbook size; sequence remaining sheets in additional batches.

**HC#6 Never auto-invoke another skill.** Adjacent-skill routing (desktop-spellcheck for spelling, viz-critique-pro-studio for tooltip content) is an opt-in handoff. Skill emits the payload; user invokes downstream.

**HC#7 Sentinel discipline.** Use `null`, `[]`, `not_present` for missing XML fields. Never blank fields in handoff schema.

**HC#8 Refuse to fabricate.** V-gate refuses fabricated findings or missing rule citations.

**HC#9 Partial-info handling.** If `get-dashboard-xml` returns partial results (per a known reliability gap), flag UNSCANNED for that dashboard with reason; do not proceed with incomplete evidence.

**HC#10 Adjacent-skill routing.** Text-copy quality → `desktop-spellcheck`. Tooltip content → `viz-critique-pro-studio`. Localization → `i18n-scanner`. Format drift on caption fonts → `format-drift-scanner`.

**HC#11 Default-name treatment locked.** Auto-generated names (`Dashboard \d+`, `Sheet \d+`, and locale variants) fire DC-DEFAULT-NAME-06 as Warning. Never Info. Never demoted under user pressure.

**HC#12 Never write the longform file silently.** File-save requires explicit user opt-in with path confirmation. Improvement plan lives in the file only; chat renders TL;DR + top 3 only.

**HC#13 Guide the user actively.** Silence during evaluation is a defect. Announce per-dashboard progress on 5+ dashboard runs.

**HC#14 Top-3 selection locked.** Sort by severity (Warning → Info), then dashboard enumeration order (as returned by `list-dashboards`), then rule ID ascending. Never pick top 3 by subjective importance.

**HC#15 Per-dashboard TL;DR ordering locked.** Per-dashboard TL;DR lines render in `list-dashboards` enumeration order. Never sorted by finding count, severity mix, or judgment. Fully-labeled dashboards render inline in their enumeration slot as `{Dashboard}: fully labeled`.

## Two-Tier Delivery

### Tier A: Compact chat summary (always renders)

Target under 25 lines. One-line TL;DR per dashboard, then workbook-wide top 3, then save-file offer.

```
**Caption Audit: {workbook_name}**
Dashboards audited: {N} · Total findings: {N Warnings, N Info}

Per-dashboard TL;DR:
- {Dashboard A}: {n} missing captions, {n} missing titles
- {Dashboard B}: {n} missing captions, {n} missing titles

Top 3 recommendations:
1. {one-line teaser, no rationale}
2. {one-line teaser, no rationale}
3. {one-line teaser, no rationale}

Save the full findings and Desktop-fix instructions to Downloads? (.md default, .txt option, or skip)
```

### Tier B: Full findings file (opt-in file)

Written to Downloads only when user confirms. File format .md (default) or .txt. Contents per `skill-expertise/report_template.md`:

- Header (skill version, timestamp, workbook name).
- Per-dashboard sections with every finding, rule ID cited, XML evidence quoted, and Desktop-fix instruction.
- Handoff schema payload (`caption_audit_report/1`).

File-save discipline: user opts in, format confirmed, path confirmed (Windows: `%USERPROFILE%\Downloads\`; macOS: `$HOME/Downloads/`), fresh-filename discipline on collision.

## Validation Gate (4-Check Read-Only)

**V1 Rule Coverage.** Every rule ID (DC-TITLE-01 through DC-TITLE-08) evaluated on every applicable element. Empty findings list is a legitimate outcome (workbook fully labeled).

**V2 Evidence Citation.** Every finding cites specific XML evidence from `get-dashboard-xml` or `get-worksheet-xml`. No fabricated findings.

**V3 Handoff Completeness.** Every field in `caption_audit_report/1` populated per `skill-expertise/handoff_schema.md`.

**V4 Ordering Determinism.** Top-3 recommendations rendered in the HC#14 sort order (severity → dashboard enum order → rule ID ascending). Per-dashboard TL;DR rendered in HC#15 order (`list-dashboards` enumeration). Default-name findings never demoted below Warning per HC#11. Verify the on-wire report matches these ordering rules before delivery.

V-gate failure blocks delivery per HC#8.

## Tool Sequence

- **Phase 0.** `get-workbook-inventory` (never twice per run). `list-dashboards` for enumeration.
- **Phase 1.** `get-dashboard-xml` per dashboard (batched). `get-worksheet-xml` per worksheet on each dashboard (batched, 10 per parallel call).
- **Phase 2-3.** In-memory rule evaluation and report assembly. No tool calls.
- **Phase 4.** Chat delivery. No tool calls.
- **Phase 5.** File-write to Downloads only on opt-in per HC#12.

## Handoff Contract

Emits `caption_audit_report/1` per `skill-expertise/handoff_schema.md`. Consumed by:

- **dashboard-preflight.** Caption findings enrich assembly hygiene.
- **desktop-spellcheck.** After captions are added, spellcheck the new text.
- **viz-critique-pro-studio.** Domain 4 layout scoring cross-references caption presence.
- **workbook-auditor.** Caption findings deltas across runs.

## Known Limitations

- **`get-worksheet-xml` dashboard-bound-sheet reliability gap**. Some worksheets on dashboards return partial XML. HC#9 flags UNSCANNED rather than fabricating.
- **Locale variants.** Default-name regex covers English (`Dashboard \d+`, `Sheet \d+`), French (`Tableau de bord \d+`, `Feuille \d+`), Spanish (`Panel \d+`, `Hoja \d+`), and German (`Dashboard \d+`, `Blatt \d+`). Other locales require regex extension.
- Cannot evaluate caption content quality (spelling, tone, clarity) — routes to desktop-spellcheck and viz-critique-pro-studio.
- Cannot detect intentionally-hidden titles (right-click > Hide Title). XML shows `<title style=hidden>` regardless of intent; skill treats hidden title as missing per DC-TITLE-01 rule.

## Error Handling

| Failure | Response |
|---|---|
| Workbook not open | Ask: Please open the workbook youd like audited. |
| `get-workbook-inventory` fails | Retry once. If still failing, exit gracefully. |
| `get-dashboard-xml` returns partial | Flag UNSCANNED for that dashboard per HC#9. |
| `get-worksheet-xml` returns garbled | Retry once per sheet. If still failing, mark that sheet UNSCANNED. |
| Workbook has 0 dashboards | Exit with No dashboards found; nothing to audit. |
| Workbook has 10+ dashboards | Ask user to scope; default to all. |
| User asks to fix captions | Refuse per HC#1. Route to Desktop-manual instructions in the report. |
| User asks to spellcheck captions | Refuse per HC#10. Route to `desktop-spellcheck` with handoff payload. |
| User asks to audit multiple workbooks | Refuse per HC#2. Ask which workbook. |
| User asks to skip V-gate | Refuse per HC#8. |
| User asks to save file without path confirmation | Refuse per HC#12. Confirm path first. |
| User asks to demote default-name to Info | Refuse per HC#11. Warning stands. |

## Relationship to Other Skills

- **Peer to desktop-spellcheck.** Spellcheck audits text-copy correctness once captions exist; this skill audits whether captions exist at all.
- **Peer to format-drift-scanner.** Format-drift audits font family, font size, and format-string consistency on captions that exist; this skill checks completeness first.
- **Upstream of viz-planner.** Missing-caption Warning findings route to viz-planner for redesign at Rework tier.
- **Adjacent to dashboard-preflight.** Preflight audits assembly hygiene structurally; this skill audits caption completeness. Both are Phase 5 layer.

## MCP Skill Mapping

Desktop-native. No MCP dependency. Uses standard Desktop tools (`get-workbook-inventory`, `list-dashboards`, `get-dashboard-xml`, `get-worksheet-xml`).

## Graceful Degradation

These rules apply whenever something this skill needs is missing or fails. More specific rules elsewhere in this file take precedence.

- **Nothing to work on.** If no workbook is open, there is no data source, or the named calc, sheet, dashboard, or data source isn't found, stop before any other step. Say what you found (list the real names, if any) and ask the user to open the workbook or pick one. Never work on a guessed or closest-match target.
- **Tool call fails, times out, or returns empty.** Retry once, then stop retrying. Mark everything that depended on that call as not checked, continue with what you still can, and say which step failed. If the failed call was a write, stop and report the workbook's current state instead of continuing.
- **Partial results.** If any check, sheet, field, or data source wasn't evaluated, the summary says so (Partial: N of M checked; not checked: [list]). Never give a clean, ready, or PASS verdict on a partial run.
- **Reference file won't open.** Use the rules summarized in this file, say [file] unavailable; using the built-in summary, and never make up thresholds, rule IDs, or Desktop menu steps from memory.
- **Peer skill not installed.** If this skill would hand off to another skill that isn't available, say so and give the manual Desktop step instead. A handoff is never the only next step.
- **Platform gap.** If no tool can do something, say so plainly and give the manual Desktop path.
- **Failure messages.** Tell the user in plain language what was done, what wasn't, and the next step. No raw errors, stack traces, or JSON.
- **No fabrication.** Never invent fields, values, findings, or results to fill a gap left by a failed read.

# Format Drift Scanner — when to use

Source: https://tableau.github.io/tableau-ai-utilities/tableau-studio-skills/tableau-agent/content-quality/format-drift-scanner

## When to Use

- You built dashboards with multiple measures and dates and want to catch inconsistencies before publish.
- You inherited a workbook and want a sanity check on formatting consistency.
- You're prepping for a stakeholder review and want to catch drift before someone else does.

## When Not to Use

- **Text-copy correctness.** Use `desktop-spellcheck` for spelling, capitalization, typography.
- **Localization fragility.** Use `i18n-scanner` for hard-coded currency, regional date collisions, region-specific vocabulary.
- **Color palette compliance.** Not supported (pixel-visibility gap).
- **Dashboard assembly hygiene.** Use `dashboard-preflight` for zone alignment, canvas size, container nesting.
- **Chart-type selection.** Use `chart-swap-advisor` for is-this-the-right-chart-type questions.
- **Applying format changes.** All fixes are Desktop-manual per HC#1.

## Example Trigger Phrases

- "Format drift"
- "Check my formatting"
- "Audit format consistency"
- "Are my dates and numbers consistent?"
- "Check number formats"
- "Date format audit"
- "Font consistency check"

# Format Drift Scanner — SKILL.md

Source: https://tableau.github.io/tableau-ai-utilities/tableau-studio-skills/tableau-agent/content-quality/format-drift-scanner/SKILL

# Format Drift Scanner

## When to use (full trigger detail)

Audit a Tableau workbook for number, date, and font format-string drift across measure placements, date pills, and text objects. Runs a locked drift catalog (currency-symbol mismatch, decimal-places mismatch, date-format mismatch, thousands-separator mismatch, font-family drift, font-size drift, negative-number-treatment drift) per data source per workbook, groups findings by drift type and severity, and produces a Desktop-fix report. Rescoped 2026-09-10 from format-consistency-scanner. number/date/font format-string drift only, no palette compliance (pixel-visibility blocked). Trigger with format drift, check my formatting, audit format consistency, are my dates and numbers consistent, format-drift-scanner, check number formats, date format audit. Do NOT trigger on.

## Purpose

Scan a Tableau workbook for format-string drift across every measure placement, date pill, and text object. Read-only. Every finding cites a locked drift-type rule and produces a Desktop-fix instruction, never a mutation.

Positioned parallel to desktop-spellcheck and i18n-scanner in the pipeline. Spellcheck owns text-copy correctness. i18n-scanner owns locale-fragility. Format Drift Scanner owns cross-worksheet format-string consistency (number formats, date formats, font families and sizes).

**Scope note (2026-09-10 rescope):** This skill was originally scoped as format-consistency-scanner with palette compliance as a fourth check. Palette compliance was dropped because color style-rules are silently dropped on apply and pixel-level color inspection is not available. Current scope is number-string, date-string, and font drift only.

## Trigger Conditions

- format drift
- check my formatting
- audit format consistency
- are my dates and numbers consistent
- format-drift-scanner
- check number formats
- date format audit
- font consistency check

## Do NOT Trigger On

- Text-copy correctness like spelling and typography (defer to `desktop-spellcheck`).
- Localization fragility, hard-coded currency, regional date-format collisions (defer to `i18n-scanner`).
- Applying format changes (all fixes are Desktop-manual per HC#1).
- Dashboard assembly hygiene (defer to `dashboard-preflight`).
- Chart-type selection (defer to `chart-swap-advisor`).
- Whole-workbook pre-publish hygiene (defer to `publish-readiness`).
- Change-over-time (defer to `workbook-auditor`).
- Data-quality issues in the underlying data (defer to `data-quality-review`).
- Calc-behind-the-format authoring (defer to calc-orchestrator).

## Scope Boundaries

- **IN.** Number format-string drift audit across every measure placement per data source. Date format-string drift audit across every date pill. Font family and font size drift audit across text objects, axis labels, tooltip labels, and worksheet titles. Locked severity tiers per drift catalog. Read-only output. Handoff schema `format_drift_report/1`.
- **OUT.** Any workbook mutation. Applying any format change. Palette / color compliance. Rendered visual output evaluation (pixel-level anything). Locale fragility. Text correctness. Whole-workbook governance.

**Cross-datasource workbooks.** Number format drift is per-DS-scoped: a currency-symbol mismatch on DS-A does not fire against DS-B. Date format drift is per-DS-scoped too. Font drift is workbook-scoped (fonts are UI-level, not DS-scoped). Cross-DS format drift produces a distinct finding severity: Info-tier when a legitimate business reason (multi-currency reporting) explains the difference, Warning-tier when no rationale is documented.

**Scale bands.**

- **Tiny (<10 measure placements).** Full audit. No batching needed.
- **Typical (10-50 placements).** Full audit. Batching per Tool Sequence.
- **Wide (50-100 placements).** Full audit. Info findings collapse into a `<details>` block after the first 5 per drift type.
- **Very wide (100+ placements).** Full audit. Warn user up-front of longer runtime. `get-worksheet-xml` batches capped at 10 worksheets per parallel call regardless of workbook size (per Tool Sequence). Offer to scope by data source or drift-type per HC#5; if the user declines to scope and the workbook exceeds 300 placements, proceed but cap Info-tier findings rendered inline at 5 per drift type (per Overflow Handling in `skill-expertise/report_template.md`) rather than holding the full set in context.

## Workflow Phases

- **Phase 0 Scope.** Confirm workbook is open. Reuse `get-workbook-inventory` output if a prior skill already called it. **Prior-report reuse:** if a `format_drift_report/1` handoff exists in session context or on disk, offer to diff. Diff-mode trigger map:
  - Measure count changed since prior report → full re-scan.
  - Date-pill count on any worksheet changed → full re-scan.
  - Any worksheet renamed, added, or removed → full re-scan.
  - User session references a format fix (I just aligned the currency symbols on Sales) → re-scan the affected drift type.
  - If none of the above changed, reuse prior findings verbatim and note diff-mode in the report.
- **Phase 1 Inventory.** Enumerate every measure placement (via `search-workbook-fields` for shelf placements), every date pill (via `get-worksheet-xml`), and every text object with a font declaration (via `get-worksheet-xml` and `get-dashboard-xml`). Multi-DS workbooks inventory per DS.
- **Phase 2 Extract Format Strings.** For each measure placement, capture the resolved format string from the worksheet XML. For each date pill, capture the date-format string. For each text object, capture font family and font size.
- **Phase 3 Detect Drift.** Compare format strings within each drift type per the classification rules in `skill-expertise/drift_catalog.md`. First finding for a drift type establishes the baseline; subsequent format strings that differ fire the drift rule.
- **Phase 4 Assemble Report.** Group findings by drift type (Currency, Decimals, Date, Separator, Font Family, Font Size, Negative Treatment) and severity (Blocking, Warning, Info). Every finding includes a Desktop-fix instruction. Report shape follows `skill-expertise/report_template.md`.
- **Phase 5 Deliver.** Compact chat summary first (drift-type counts + top 3 findings). Offer to write the full report to Downloads (`.md` or `.txt`).

## The 7-Drift Catalog

Full detail lives in `skill-expertise/drift_catalog.md`. Summary:

1. **F-CURRENCY-01 Currency-Symbol Mismatch.** Measures within the same DS use inconsistent currency symbols ($, €, £, ¥, etc.) or mix formatted-currency with plain-number formatting.
2. **F-DECIMAL-02 Decimal-Places Mismatch.** Same measure appears with different decimal-place formats across worksheets (SUM(Sales) shows as $1,234 on one sheet and $1,234.56 on another).
3. **F-DATE-03 Date-Format Mismatch.** Same date field renders with different format strings across worksheets (MM/DD/YYYY on one, DD-MMM-YYYY on another, YYYY-MM-DD on a third).
4. **F-SEPARATOR-04 Thousands-Separator Mismatch.** Same measure uses inconsistent thousands separators (1,234 vs 1234 vs 1 234 vs 1.234).
5. **F-FONT-FAMILY-05 Font-Family Drift.** Multiple font families used across text objects, axis labels, tooltips, or worksheet titles without a stated design rationale.
6. **F-FONT-SIZE-06 Font-Size Drift.** Font sizes vary across similar text elements (worksheet titles at 12pt on some sheets and 14pt on others; tooltip labels at 9pt vs 11pt).
7. **F-NEGATIVE-07 Negative-Number-Treatment Drift.** Negative numbers rendered inconsistently (parentheses `(1,234)` vs minus-sign `-1,234` vs red-color vs both).

## Hard Constraints

**HC#1 Read-only always.** Never invoke `author-calc`, `bind-template`, `build-and-apply-worksheet`, or any mutating tool. Every finding is a Desktop-fix instruction the user applies manually via right-click > Format > select field/axis/tooltip > adjust.

**HC#2 One workbook per run.** Multi-workbook audits are refused. Users invoke separately per workbook.

**HC#3 Bulk-action refusal.** If the user asks to fix all format drift or align every currency symbol, refuse and route: format changes are Desktop-manual per HC#1.

**HC#4 No fabricated findings.** Every finding cites a specific drift-catalog rule ID (F-CURRENCY-01 through F-NEGATIVE-07) with the specific format strings that differ. If a format string cannot be read (e.g., `get-worksheet-xml` fails on a dashboard-bound sheet), flag UNSCANNED with `reason: fallback_unavailable`.

**HC#5 User-named-drift-type wins.** If the user asks for just check the date-format drift or audit only currency symbols, run only the specified drift type and skip the rest.

**HC#6 Never localize.** Locale-fragility (regional date-format collisions, hard-coded currency for global audiences) routes to i18n-scanner. Drift Scanner treats format strings as-authored, not as-locale-appropriate.

**HC#7 Sentinel discipline.** Use `null`, `[]`, `unscanned` for missing data. Never blank fields in the handoff schema.

**HC#8 Refuse to fabricate.** If the V-gate cannot pass after one retry, refuse delivery and diagnose. Never fake a V-gate pass.

**HC#9 Partial-info handling.** If the ask includes partial context (audit format drift but skip the fonts), deliver on the specified drift types and note which were skipped.

**HC#10 Adjacent-skill routing.** Text-copy correctness routes to `desktop-spellcheck`. Locale fragility routes to `i18n-scanner`. Dashboard assembly hygiene routes to `dashboard-preflight`. Chart-type selection routes to `chart-swap-advisor`.

**HC#11 Baseline-first classification.** For each drift type within a DS scope (or workbook scope for fonts), the first observed format string becomes the baseline. Subsequent format strings that differ fire the drift rule. Never invent a synthetic baseline; use the first-seen format string.

**HC#12 Cross-DS drift is Info-by-default.** Same measure name across different data sources with different formats is Info-tier, not Warning, unless a rationale is missing from the workbook caption. Multi-currency reporting is a legitimate use case; drift within one DS is not.

## Common Mistakes

Behaviors this skill must never exhibit, even under user pressure:

1. **Inferring drift from field name alone.** Two measures named Sales on different worksheets are not automatically a mismatch; read the actual format strings from XML. Names are user-authored and unreliable.
2. **Fabricating a drift finding to fill an empty severity band.** If Blocking count is zero, render `_None._`. Never invent a fake drift finding.
3. **Rewriting the drift catalog mid-run.** The 7-drift catalog and severity assignments are locked in `skill-expertise/drift_catalog.md`.
4. **Silently skipping placements that fail `get-worksheet-xml`.** Every placement identified in Phase 1 must appear in the report, even if downstream format-string extraction fails. Missing placements are UNSCANNED, not omitted.
5. **Applying a fix in Desktop.** All findings are Desktop-manual per HC#1. Never invoke `author-calc`, `bind-template`, or any mutating tool.
6. **Confusing legitimate multi-currency reporting with drift.** Cross-DS format differences with a documented rationale are Info-tier, not Warning per HC#12.
7. **Treating font-family drift as always-Warning.** Two font families for the same element category (e.g., Tableau Light for KPIs vs Tableau Book for body text) is a legitimate design choice when documented. Undocumented drift is the Warning case.

## Validation Gate (3-Check Read-Only)

**V1 Format-String Completeness.** Every measure placement, date pill, and text object identified in Phase 1 has a resolved format string in Phase 2 (or sentinel `unscanned` with rationale). No placements silently omitted.

**V2 Drift-Catalog Match.** Every finding references a specific catalog rule ID (F-CURRENCY-01 through F-NEGATIVE-07) with the two-or-more differing format strings that fired the rule.

**V3 Handoff Completeness.** Every field in `format_drift_report/1` populated per `skill-expertise/handoff_schema.md`. Sentinel values acceptable per HC#7.

Any V-gate failure blocks delivery per HC#8. Fail-open is NOT applied since the skill is read-only.

## Tool Sequence

Locked sequence to minimize latency and honor tool dependencies.

- **Phase 0.** Reuse session-context `get-workbook-inventory` if available. Otherwise, call `get-workbook-inventory` + `list-worksheets` + `list-dashboards` + `list-workbook-data-sources` in parallel.
- **Phase 1.** `list-available-fields` (verbosity: full) per DS in parallel. `search-workbook-fields` for shelf placements per measure. Batch worksheet XML reads (`get-worksheet-xml`) in groups of ~10 with inline progress notes for workbooks with 30+ worksheets.
- **Phase 2.** Extract format strings from Phase 1 XML in memory. No additional tool calls.
- **Phase 3-4.** In-memory drift detection and assembly. No tool calls.
- **Phase 5.** No tool calls unless file-write opted in.

**Batching rules.**

- Never call `get-workbook-inventory` twice per run.
- Never call `list-available-fields` twice per DS unless truncated.
- `get-worksheet-xml` called once per worksheet. Reuse session-context reads from prior skills.
- `resolve-field` only when a fields DS scope is ambiguous.

**Early-exit condition.** If Phase 1 inventory returns zero measure placements AND zero date pills AND zero text objects, skip Phases 2-4, deliver no formattable elements in this workbook report.

## Handoff Contract

Emits `format_drift_report/1` per `skill-expertise/handoff_schema.md`. Consumed by:

- **publish-readiness.** Format drift counts inform pre-publish hygiene summary.
- **workbook-auditor.** Format-drift findings enrich change digests when the user aligns formats.
- **i18n-scanner.** Format drift findings that overlap with locale patterns are noted (e.g., `$` symbol at the currency drift level is a candidate locale finding).

## Known Limitations

- `get-worksheet-xml` reliability on dashboard-bound populated sheets (platform gap). Fallback: use `list-available-fields` metadata (limited format-string surface). Placements flagged UNSCANNED when fallback fails.
- Cannot detect rendered visual differences that are not encoded in the format string (e.g., a locale override at render time).
- Cannot detect font drift on chart marks (mark labels vs. axis labels) when the underlying mark type doesnt expose font attributes in XML.
- One workbook per run. Batching refused per HC#3.

## Error Handling

| Failure | Response |
|---|---|
| `get-workbook-inventory` fails | Report tool failure, ask user to reopen workbook. Do not proceed. |
| `list-available-fields` fails | Retry once. If still failing, refuse delivery and diagnose. Do not partially inventory. |
| `get-worksheet-xml` fails on dashboard-bound sheet | Fallback to `list-available-fields` metadata. Flag partial placements as UNSCANNED with `reason: fallback_unavailable`. |
| `get-dashboard-xml` fails | Flag dashboard-level text-object findings as UNSCANNED. Continue with worksheet-level checks. |
| `search-workbook-fields` fails | Flag shelf-placement-count findings as UNSCANNED. Continue with format-string audit on any placements found via `get-worksheet-xml` direct reads. |
| Datasource disconnects mid-run | Flag every check depending on that DS as UNSCANNED with `reason: tool_failure`. Continue with DS-independent checks (font drift). |
| Field-level permission denial (RLS) blocks a measure | Flag the specific placement UNSCANNED with `reason: fallback_unavailable`. Never treat as absence. |
| Workbook has zero measure placements AND zero date pills AND zero text objects | Report no formattable elements in this workbook. Suggest viz-planner or worksheet-builder. |
| User asks to align formats automatically | Refuse per HC#1 and HC#3. Route to Desktop UI (Format pane) with the list of drift findings. |
| User asks about color palette drift | Refuse per HC#10 and scope note. |
| User asks about text spelling | Refuse per HC#10. Route to desktop-spellcheck. |
| User asks about locale fragility | Refuse per HC#10. Route to i18n-scanner. |

## Examples

**Example 1: Clean workbook.** User: Check my formatting. Agent inventories 45 measure placements, 12 date pills, 28 text objects across 3 data sources. All format strings within each drift category align. Reports 0 Blocking, 0 Warning, 0 Info. Format-string consistency across all 3 data sources and 8 worksheets. Emits handoff.

**Example 2: Currency-symbol drift.** User: Are my numbers consistent? Agent finds SUM(Sales) formatted as `$#,##0` on one worksheet and `#,##0` (no currency) on another within the same DS. Reports F-CURRENCY-01 Warning with the two format strings and the Desktop-fix: Right-click SUM(Sales) on the affected worksheet > Format > Numbers > Currency (Custom).

**Example 3: Cross-DS Info.** User: Format drift audit. Agent finds Sales measure formatted as `$#,##0` in USD DS and `€#,##0` in EUR DS. Reports F-CURRENCY-01 Info (not Warning) per HC#12: Multi-DS currency difference detected. Not flagged as drift; documented as legitimate multi-currency reporting.

**Example 4: Bulk-action refusal.** User: Fix all format drift. Agent refuses per HC#1 and HC#3: Format changes are Desktop-manual. I can list every drift finding with the specific right-click > Format path, and you apply each in Desktop. Want the full list?

**Example 5: Scoped audit (HC#5).** User: Just check the date formats. Agent runs F-DATE-03 only, reports drift findings for date pills only, notes in the handoff that other drift types were skipped by user request.

## Relationship to Other Skills

- **Peer to desktop-spellcheck.** Spellcheck owns text-copy correctness. Format Drift Scanner owns format-string consistency.
- **Peer to i18n-scanner.** i18n-scanner owns locale-fragility. Format Drift Scanner owns cross-worksheet drift regardless of locale.
- **Upstream of publish-readiness.** Drift findings inform pre-publish hygiene.
- **Adjacent to dashboard-preflight.** Preflight owns assembly hygiene. Drift Scanner owns format-string hygiene.
- **Never overlaps with data-quality-review, data-scribe, calc-family, or worksheet-builder.**

## MCP Skill Mapping

Desktop-native. No MCP dependency.

# Tableau Caption and Tooltip Advisor — when to use

Source: https://tableau.github.io/tableau-ai-utilities/tableau-studio-skills/tableau-agent/content-quality/caption-and-tooltip-advisor

## What it does

Reads a live dashboard (titles, captions, tooltips, axis labels) and audits every text surface against a locked 6-rule catalog. For each weak surface, proposes a rewrite in the author's declared audience voice and gives numbered Desktop steps to apply it. Author owns execution; the skill never mutates the workbook.

Two modes. **Audit mode** returns a full severity-ranked finding list with before/after rewrites. **Rewrite-suggestions-only mode** returns the rewrites compressed by sheet with one combined Desktop-steps block at the end, for authors who already know what is wrong and just want the proposed text.

Pairs with dashboard-caption-audit (presence check), spellcheck (typo check), viz-critique-pro-studio (whole-dashboard scoring), and stakeholder-translator (plain-language translation) as optional downstream routes with manual fallbacks.

## When to use it

- "I built this dashboard and the tooltips show `SUM(Sales)` instead of a real label."
- "My dashboard title is still 'Insert title here' and I need to fix it before the review."
- "The tooltip template on this chart has raw `[Field]` references the viewer sees."
- "I want to rewrite the captions for an executive audience, not an analyst audience."
- "I want just the rewrites grouped by sheet, not a full severity report."

## When NOT to use it

- Not for presence-only audits (use dashboard-caption-audit)
- Not for typo-only checks (use spellcheck)
- Not for whole-dashboard critique (use viz-critique-pro-studio)
- Not for a plain-language translation of what the dashboard answers (use stakeholder-translator)
- Not for authoring or editing anything in Desktop (this skill is read-only advisory)

## How to trigger it

- "rewrite my tooltips"
- "fix my captions"
- "my tooltips look weird"
- "better tooltip text"
- "SUM of sales in tooltip looks ugly"
- "tooltip and caption review"
- "my labels are bad"
